temas.regla: To say every + a time word, use cada + singular noun (cada día, cada semana) or todos los / todas las + plural noun (todos los días, todas las semanas). Both mean the same.
temas.titulo: Cada and todos los for every (time)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Quantitative adjective in Spanish: cada and todos/-as for "every" in time phrases (Adjetivo cuantitativo)

temas.regla: This and these before a noun: este + masculine singular, esta + feminine singular, estos + masculine plural, estas + feminine plural. They agree with the noun.
temas.titulo: Este, esta, estos, estas (this, these)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Demonstrative adjectives: este, esta, estos, estas to say this/these in Spanish (Adjetivos demostrativos)

temas.regla: To make an adverb, add -mente to the feminine singular form of the adjective: rápida → rápidamente. Adjectives with one form just add -mente: fácil → fácilmente. A written accent on the adjective stays.
temas.titulo: Adverbs ending in -mente
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming regular adverbs ending in -mente in Spanish

temas.regla: My, your, his, her, its, our, their before a noun: mi, tu, su, nuestro. They agree with the thing owned, not the owner: add -s for plural things (mis amigos), and nuestro also changes for gender (nuestra casa). Su means his, her, its, their and your (usted, ustedes).
temas.titulo: Possessive adjectives: mi, tu, su, nuestro
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Possessive adjectives in Spanish: my, your, his, her, its, our and their (Adjetivos posesivos)

temas.regla: Nationality and origin adjectives ending in -és add -a for the feminine and lose the written accent: inglés → inglesa, francés → francesa. They are written in lowercase.
temas.titulo: Feminine of nationalities ending in -s
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the singular feminine of -s ending nationality and place of origin adjectives in Spanish

temas.regla: Nationality and origin adjectives ending in -és form the masculine plural with -eses (inglés → ingleses) and the feminine plural with -esas (inglesas). The written accent disappears. A mixed group takes the masculine.
temas.titulo: Plural of nationalities ending in -s
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the plural of -s ending nationality and place of origin adjectives in Spanish

temas.regla: Cada + singular noun = each. Cada never changes for gender or number, takes no article, and the verb is singular: cada alumno tiene, cada casa tiene.
temas.titulo: Cada + noun (each)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Quantitative adjective in Spanish: cada + noun for each (Adjetivo cuantitativo)

temas.regla: To ask when, use ¿Cuándo + verb + subject? Cuándo always has a written accent in questions, and the verb comes right after it. For an exact clock time, ask ¿A qué hora?
temas.titulo: How to ask when: ¿cuándo?
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to ask "When" in Spanish

temas.regla: Most adjectives ending in -e, and those ending in -a (like optimista), have one form for masculine and feminine singular: un chavo inteligente, una chava inteligente; un hombre optimista, una mujer optimista.
temas.titulo: Adjectives ending in -e and -a
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the singular masculine and feminine of adjectives ending -e and -a in Spanish

temas.regla: Adjectives ending in -e or -a (grande, idealista) have one form for masculine and feminine. To make them plural, just add -s: grandes, idealistas.
temas.titulo: Plural of adjectives in -e and -a
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the plural of masculine and feminine adjectives ending in -e and -a in Spanish

temas.regla: Ese, esa, esos, esas mean that / those: something near the listener or a bit away from the speaker. They go before the noun and agree with it in gender and number.
temas.titulo: That, those: ese, esa, esos, esas
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Demonstrative adjectives: ese, esa, esos, esas to say that/those in Spanish (Adjetivos demostrativos)

temas.regla: ¿Dónde? asks where something is or happens; ¿Adónde? (or ¿A dónde?) asks where to, with verbs of motion like ir; ¿De dónde? asks where from. In questions dónde always has an accent.
temas.titulo: Asking where: dónde, adónde, de dónde
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to ask "Where" in Spanish

temas.regla: Más (more) and menos (less, fewer) never change. Before a noun they are adjectives (más tortillas), alone they are pronouns (quiero más), and after a verb they are adverbs (corre más).
temas.titulo: Más / menos: more, less, fewer
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using más/menos for more/less/fewer in Spanish (as adjectives, pronouns and adverbs)

temas.regla: Nationality and origin adjectives ending in -e (canadiense, estadounidense, nicaragüense) have one form for masculine and feminine: they don't change.
temas.titulo: Nationalities in -e: same form for women
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the singular feminine of -e ending nationality and origin adjectives in Spanish

temas.regla: Nationality and origin adjectives ending in -e (canadiense, estadounidense) form the plural by adding -s, for masculine and feminine alike: canadienses.
temas.titulo: Plural of nationalities in -e
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the plural of -e ending nationality and origin adjectives in Spanish

temas.regla: Colors are adjectives and agree with the noun: -o colors have four forms (rojo, roja, rojos, rojas); colors in -e or a consonant only change for number (verde, verdes; azul, azules). As nouns, colors are masculine: el rojo.
temas.titulo: Colors: gender and number
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Colours in Spanish - gender and number (adjectives)

temas.regla: Dentro de + noun or pronoun = inside something: dentro de la caja. Dentro alone = inside, when the place is understood. In Mexico, adentro is very common for the same idea.
temas.titulo: Dentro / dentro de (inside)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using dentro/dentro de in Spanish (inside)

temas.regla: To say someone's name, use the reflexive verb llamarse (literally to call oneself): me llamo, te llamas, se llama, nos llamamos, se llaman. To ask, use ¿Cómo…?, not ¿Qué…?
temas.titulo: Llamarse: saying someone's name
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the verb llamarse in Spanish in the present tense to say what someone's name is (Verbo reflexivo)

temas.regla: Use ser (not estar) for what someone or something is like by nature: looks, personality, size, shape, material. Estar is for temporary states.
temas.titulo: Ser for essential characteristics
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to express an essential characteristic

temas.regla: To say where a person, a thing or a place is, use estar, never ser: ¿Dónde está el baño? Tijuana está en Baja California.
temas.titulo: Estar for location
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar in Spanish (not ser) when talking about locations

temas.regla: To say you like something, use me gusta + one thing and me gustan + several things. The thing you like is the subject, so gustar agrees with it, not with you.
temas.titulo: Gustar: to like something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using gustar in Spanish to say you like something

temas.regla: To say you like doing something, use me gusta + infinitive: me gusta surfear. It's always gusta (singular), even with two or more activities: me gusta leer y cocinar.
temas.titulo: Gustar + infinitive: to like doing
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using gustar in Spanish + verb to say like [doing something]

temas.regla: Time as an occasion (once, twice, how many times) is vez, plural veces: una vez, dos veces, muchas veces. Time as duration is tiempo.
temas.titulo: Vez / veces: once, twice, many times
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using vez/veces = time/times in Spanish

temas.regla: To say at what time something happens, use a la una for one o'clock and a las + hour for all the others: a las dos, a las ocho y media. Ask with ¿A qué hora…?
temas.titulo: A la / a las + time: at what time
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using A + la/las + [time] to say at what time something takes place in Spanish

temas.regla: To say you have to do something, use tener que + infinitive: tengo que trabajar. Conjugate tener, keep the infinitive, and never drop que.
temas.titulo: Tener que: to have to
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing obligation with tener que in Spanish

temas.regla: Deber (must, should), poder (can) and querer (to want) go straight into an infinitive, with nothing in between: debo trabajar, puedo nadar, quiero comer.
temas.titulo: Deber, poder, querer + infinitive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using deber, poder, querer in Spanish + infinitive to express must, can, to want to (Verbo modal)

temas.regla: To ask politely, soften quiero: quisiera, quería or querría + a noun or an infinitive all mean 'I would like'. Quisiera is the most polite; quería is the everyday one.
temas.titulo: Quisiera, quería, querría: I would like
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Polite requests in Spanish: querría, quería and quisiera to politely say "I would like"

temas.regla: Doler works like gustar: me duele + one thing, me duelen + several: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies. Body parts take el, la, los, las.
temas.titulo: Doler: to say something hurts
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using doler in Spanish to say that something hurts

temas.regla: To say where or when an event takes place (a party, a concert, a class), use ser, not estar: la fiesta es en mi casa, el concierto es el sábado. People and things still take estar for location.
temas.titulo: Ser for where and when events take place
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to say when / where something takes place

temas.regla: To say what time, day, date or season it is, use ser, not estar: es lunes, son las tres, hoy es 4 de mayo, es verano.
temas.titulo: Ser for time, days, dates and seasons
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to talk about time, days, dates and seasons

temas.regla: Use the simple present for things you do regularly: routines and habits. Words like siempre, todos los días or los lunes often go with it.
temas.titulo: Present tense for regular actions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the present tense in Spanish to talk about regular actions (El Presente)

temas.regla: To introduce someone (or yourself), use ser: soy Claude, este es Beto, esta es mi hermana, estos son mis papás. Never estar.
temas.titulo: Ser to introduce people
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to introduce people

temas.regla: Necesitar is a regular -ar verb. Use necesitar + a noun for something you need, and necesitar + an infinitive for something you need to do, with nothing in between.
temas.titulo: Necesitar to express a need
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using necesitar in the present tense to express a need (to do something) in Spanish

temas.regla: To say what someone does for a living, use ser + the profession, with no un or una: soy cerrajero, es doctora. Never estar.
temas.titulo: Ser for professions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to say what you do for a living

temas.regla: To say how people are related (family, friends, partners, coworkers), use ser: es mi hermana, somos amigos, son novios.
temas.titulo: Ser for relationships
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to describe relationships

temas.regla: For nationality and origin, use ser: ser + nationality (soy mexicano) or ser de + place (soy de Tijuana). Nationalities are lowercase and agree with the person.
temas.titulo: Ser for origin and nationality
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to express origin or nationality

temas.regla: Use hay to say that something exists (with un, una, numbers, mucho or no article). Use está / están to say where a specific thing is (with el, la, mi, a name).
temas.titulo: Hay vs está
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between hay and está in Spanish

temas.regla: Ask ¿Qué hora es? Answer with es la una (1:00 to 1:59) and son las + number for every other hour, then add y + minutes, y cuarto, y media or menos + minutes.
temas.titulo: Telling the time
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Telling the time in Spanish

temas.regla: Most weather phrases use hace + noun: hace calor, hace frío, hace sol, hace viento, hace buen tiempo. Since calor and frío are nouns, very is mucho, not muy.
temas.titulo: Hace for the weather
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using hace to talk about the weather in Spanish

temas.regla: Talk about the weather with hay + noun (hay niebla), está + adjective or -ndo form (está nublado, está lloviendo), or a weather verb on its own (llueve, nieva). Weather verbs have no subject and only use the él form.
temas.titulo: Weather with hay, está or a weather verb
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using hay, está, or an impersonal verb to talk about the weather in Spanish

temas.regla: To identify something, to say what or who it is, use ser + noun: es un libro, es mi casa, son tacos. Never estar.
temas.titulo: Ser (not estar) to say what something is
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser in Spanish (not estar) to identify things

temas.regla: Many nouns for people and animals end in -o for males and -a for females (el hijo, la hija); nouns ending in a consonant add -a (el doctor, la doctora). Plural: add -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant. A mixed group uses the masculine plural.
temas.titulo: Masculine and feminine nouns: -o and -a
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming regular masculine and feminine nouns in Spanish (singular and plural)

temas.regla: A + el always becomes al, and de + el always becomes del. Only with el: a la, a los, a las, de la, de los, de las never contract, and neither does él (he).
temas.titulo: Al and del: a + el, de + el
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Al and Del in Spanish

temas.regla: Nouns ending in a consonant (except -z) can be masculine (el árbol) or feminine (la flor), so learn the article with the noun. Plural: add -es (los árboles, las flores), and watch the written accent.
temas.titulo: Nouns ending in a consonant
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender and number of nouns ending in a consonant in Spanish (except -z)

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -e can be masculine (el puente, el nombre) or feminine (la calle, la gente), so learn the article with the noun. Plural: add -s. La gente is singular: la gente es.
temas.titulo: Nouns ending in -e
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender and plural of nouns ending in -e in Spanish

temas.regla: Unos and unas are the plural of un and una: unos + masculine plural, unas + feminine plural. They mean some or a few with things you can count.
temas.titulo: Unos, unas: some, a few
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using unos, unas + plural nouns to say some / a few in Spanish (Artículo indefinido -plural)

temas.regla: Numbers go before the noun and don't change, except uno (un before a masculine noun, una before a feminine one, also in 21, 31…) and the hundreds (doscientos, doscientas). From two up, the noun is plural.
temas.titulo: Numbers with nouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using numbers with nouns in Spanish

temas.regla: Months are masculine and written in lowercase. They usually go without an article (en mayo); when one is needed, it's masculine: un enero frío, el diciembre pasado.
temas.titulo: Months are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Months in Spanish: masculine

temas.regla: Days of the week are masculine (el lunes, este domingo, todos los martes) and lowercase. Lunes to viernes are the same in the plural (los lunes); sábado and domingo add -s.
temas.titulo: Days of the week are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Days of the week in Spanish are masculine

temas.regla: The cardinal points (norte, sur, este, oeste and their mixes) are masculine nouns, so they take el, and a + el / de + el contract to al / del.
temas.titulo: Cardinal points are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Cardinal points in Spanish are masculine

temas.regla: When you talk about a number itself (the figure, a grade, a lucky number), it is a masculine noun: el siete, un diez, los ochos.
temas.titulo: Numbers are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Numbers in Spanish: masculine

temas.regla: For people and animals, the female form is made in different ways: changing -o to -a (gato / gata), adding -a (león / leona), using a different word (toro / vaca), or keeping one word and changing only the article (el / la estudiante). Some animals have one gender for both sexes (la ballena, el tiburón): add macho or hembra.
temas.titulo: Gender of living creatures
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender of living creatures in Spanish

temas.regla: With body parts and clothing, Spanish uses el, la, los, las (not mi, tu, su) when it's already clear whose they are, usually because a pronoun like me, te or se already tells you.
temas.titulo: Articles with body parts and clothing
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using definite articles el, la, los, las in Spanish with bodyparts and clothing (Artículo definido)

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -z form the plural by changing z to c and adding -es: la luz → las luces, la vez → las veces.
temas.titulo: Plural of nouns in -z
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the plural of nouns ending in -z in Spanish

temas.regla: Letters of the alphabet are feminine, because they stand for la letra: la a, la eme, una hache. This stays true even for letters starting with a stressed a sound: la a, la hache, not el.
temas.titulo: Letters of the alphabet are feminine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Letters of the alphabet in Spanish: feminine

temas.regla: Dates follow el + number + de + month (+ de + year): el 4 de mayo de 2026. Use plain numbers, except that the 1st is often el primero. Months are lowercase, and el already means on.
temas.titulo: Expressing dates
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing dates in Spanish

temas.regla: To say on which day something happens, put el before the day for one occasion (el lunes = on Monday) and los for a habit (los lunes = on Mondays). Never use en.
temas.titulo: The article with days of the week
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the definite article with days of the week for events

temas.regla: To make a sentence negative, put no right before the verb. If there's an object or reflexive pronoun (me, te, lo, se…), no goes before the pronoun: no lo sé, no me gusta.
temas.titulo: Negative sentences with no
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming negative sentences using no in Spanish (negation)

temas.regla: Who is quién for one person and quiénes for more than one, always with an accent in questions. Any preposition goes in front: ¿con quién?, ¿para quién?, and ¿de quién? means whose.
temas.titulo: How to ask "who"
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to ask "who" in Spanish

temas.regla: In Mexico and most of Latin America, cuál (plural cuáles) can go straight before a noun to ask which one(s) from a set: ¿Cuál carro? Qué + noun means the same and is correct everywhere.
temas.titulo: Cuál + noun in questions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cuál in Spanish followed by a noun in interrogative sentences

temas.regla: Qué means what. In questions it always carries an accent, and it goes first in the question, or right after its preposition: ¿Qué quieres? ¿De qué hablas?
temas.titulo: Questions with qué (what)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming questions with qué in Spanish = what (LatAm)

temas.regla: Before a verb, qué asks for a definition or open information (¿Qué es un burrito?), while cuál (plural cuáles) asks you to pick or identify a specific one (¿Cuál es tu número?). Both translate as what or which.
temas.titulo: Qué vs cuál + verb
temas.titulo_kwiziq: What vs Which in Spanish: qué vs cuál + verb

temas.regla: To say what something is for, or why you do something (in order to), use para: para + infinitive or para + noun. Never por for a purpose or goal.
temas.titulo: Para for purpose
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs para in Spanish: Using para (and not por) for purpose, goal or objective

temas.regla: Spanish has no 's. To say whose something is, use thing + de + owner: la tabla de Beto. De + el contracts to del.
temas.titulo: De for possession
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using preposition de in Spanish to express possession

temas.regla: Noun + de + noun describes what something is made of, what kind it is or what it contains: una mesa de madera, la clase de historia, un vaso de agua. The second noun has no article.
temas.titulo: De for description
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the preposition "de" in Spanish with nouns for description

temas.regla: Con means with: who you're with, what you use, what something comes with, and how you do it. With mí and ti it becomes conmigo and contigo.
temas.titulo: Con = with
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "con" in Spanish (with) - General use

temas.regla: A means to: it marks where you're going (voy a la playa), the clock time something happens (a las tres) and the person who receives something (le doy el libro a Ana). A + el contracts to al.
temas.titulo: A = to
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "a" in Spanish (to) - general use

temas.regla: En means in, on, inside or at for where someone or something is (estoy en casa, las llaves están en la mesa). It also goes with transport (en camión), months and years (en octubre).
temas.titulo: En = in, on, at
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "en" in Spanish (on/in/inside/at) - general use

temas.regla: Sin means without. Use sin + noun (usually with no article: café sin azúcar) or sin + infinitive where English uses -ing (se fue sin decir nada).
temas.titulo: Sin = without
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "sin" in Spanish (without) - General use

temas.regla: Sobre means on / on top of (touching), above / over (not touching), and about (a topic).
temas.titulo: The preposition sobre (on, above, about)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "sobre" in Spanish (on/on top of/above/about) - general use

temas.regla: Entre means between (two things, places or times) and among (a group). With pronouns it takes tú and yo: entre tú y yo.
temas.titulo: The preposition entre (between, among)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "entre" in Spanish (between/among) - general use

temas.regla: Hacia means towards (a direction, without saying you arrive), around (an approximate time: hacia las ocho) and towards a person (feelings).
temas.titulo: The preposition hacia (towards, around)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "hacia" in Spanish (towards/around) - general use

temas.regla: Contra means against: touching or leaning on something, playing or fighting someone, and opposing something. To be against an idea: estar en contra de.
temas.titulo: The preposition contra (against)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "contra" in Spanish (against) - General use

temas.regla: In the morning / afternoon / night: en la or por la + mañana, tarde, noche. With a clock time, use de: a las seis de la mañana.
temas.titulo: Parts of the day: en la / por la mañana
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using en/a/por in Spanish to express a part of the day

temas.regla: Tú with an accent is the pronoun you. Tu without an accent is your and always goes before a noun; its plural is tus.
temas.titulo: Tú vs tu (you vs your)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between tú and tu in Spanish (you and your) (singular informal)

temas.regla: Use tú with friends, family, kids and people your age; usted with older people, strangers, bosses and customers. Usted takes the él/ella verb form, and your is su. For more than one person, use ustedes.
temas.titulo: Tú vs usted (informal vs formal)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Tú vs Usted in Spanish (informal vs formal)

temas.regla: Él with an accent is the pronoun he / him. El without an accent is the article the. A + el and de + el contract to al and del, but a él and de él never do.
temas.titulo: Él vs el (he vs the)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between él and el in Spanish (he or the)

temas.regla: Spanish has three distances: este (this, near me), ese (that, near you or a little away) and aquel (that over there, far from both of us). All three go before the noun and agree with it in gender and number.
temas.titulo: This, that, that over there: este, ese, aquel
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between este, ese and aquel (demonstrative adjectives)

temas.regla: To compare two unequal things, put más (more) or menos (less) before the adjective, adverb or noun, and que (than) before the second thing. With a verb, más / menos goes right after the verb: corro más que tú.
temas.titulo: More … than, less … than: más … que, menos … que
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Use [verb] más [adjective/noun] que / menos [adjective/noun] que = more...than / less... than (comparatives)

temas.regla: To say two things are equal in a quality, use tan + adjective or adverb + como. Tan never changes; the adjective agrees with what it describes.
temas.titulo: As … as: tan … como
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using tan ... como = as ... as (comparatives with adjectives and adverbs)

temas.regla: With a noun, use tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + como, agreeing with the noun. With a verb, use verb + tanto como, and tanto never changes.
temas.titulo: As much / as many as: tanto como
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using tanto como with verbs and nouns to say as much/many ... as (comparatives)

temas.regla: Before a noun, demasiado, bastante, suficiente, poco, tanto and mucho agree with it. Demasiado, mucho, poco and tanto have four forms; bastante and suficiente only change for number.
temas.titulo: Quantity words: demasiado, bastante, suficiente, poco, tanto, mucho
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using demasiado, bastante, suficiente, poco, tanto and mucho to express quantity in Spanish (quantitative adjectives)

temas.regla: Aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas mean that / those (over there): something far from both the speaker and the listener, in space or in time. They go before the noun and agree with it.
temas.titulo: That, those (over there): aquel, aquella
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Demonstrative adjectives: aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas = that/those in Spanish [over there] (Adjetivos demostrativos)

temas.regla: Before a noun, algún / alguna (singular) mean some, any or a; algunos / algunas (plural) mean some or a few. Alguno drops its -o before a masculine singular noun: algún día.
temas.titulo: Some, any: algún, alguna, algunos, algunas
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using algún (a, as, os) to say some or any in Spanish

temas.regla: To say not any or no + noun, use no + verb + ningún (masculine) or ninguna (feminine) + a singular noun. Spanish keeps both negatives, and ninguno drops its -o before a masculine noun.
temas.titulo: Not any: ningún, ninguna
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the negative ningún (a, os, as) = not any

temas.regla: Four comparatives are irregular: mejor (better), peor (worse), mayor (older) and menor (younger). They are the same for masculine and feminine, add -es in the plural, and take que: mejor que tú.
temas.titulo: Better, worse, older, younger: mejor, peor, mayor, menor
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming comparative adjectives in Spanish: mayor/menor/mejor/peor

temas.regla: Adjectives ending in -z or -l have the same singular form for masculine and feminine: un carro azul, una casa azul. The exception is nationality and origin words, which add -a: español → española.
temas.titulo: Adjectives in -z and -l: one form for both genders
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the singular of masculine and feminine adjectives ending in -z and -l

temas.regla: Adjectives ending in -z or -l have one form for masculine and feminine. In the plural, -z becomes -ces and -l adds -es: feliz → felices, fácil → fáciles.
temas.titulo: Plural of adjectives in -z and -l
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the plural of masculine and feminine Spanish adjectives ending in -z and -l

temas.regla: Adjectives ending in -án, -ón and -or add -a for the feminine and -es / -as for the plural, and the written accent of -án and -ón disappears: llorón → llorona, llorones, lloronas. Comparatives like mayor, menor, mejor and peor don't take -a.
temas.titulo: Adjectives in -án, -ón, -or
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the singular and plural of adjectives ending in -án, ón, -or

temas.regla: When ningún / ninguna + noun comes before the verb, it means no + noun and you don't add no: Ningún alumno vino. If it comes after the verb, you need no before the verb: No vino ningún alumno.
temas.titulo: Ningún / ninguna + noun before the verb
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ningún, ninguna + noun + verb = No [noun] + verb (negation)

temas.regla: Used as adverbs (with an adjective, an adverb or a verb), demasiado, bastante, un poco, mucho, muy, tan and tanto never change form. Muy and tan go before adjectives and adverbs; mucho and tanto go with verbs; demasiado, bastante and un poco work with both.
temas.titulo: Demasiado, bastante, un poco, mucho, muy, tan, tanto
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using demasiado, bastante, un poco, mucho, tan, tanto and muy for too, quite, a bit, so, so much and very in Spanish (quantitative adverbs)

temas.regla: Todo agrees with the noun and goes before the article: todo el / toda la + singular = the whole, all; todos los / todas las + plural = all, every. The article (or a possessive or demonstrative) can't be dropped.
temas.titulo: Todo, toda, todos, todas (all, every, the whole)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using todo, toda, todos and todas to say all, every and the whole (indefinite adjectives)

temas.regla: Otro agrees with the noun (otro, otra, otros, otras) and never takes un / una: otro café = another coffee. It can follow el, la, mis, etc. (el otro día), and it goes before numbers: otros dos = two more.
temas.titulo: Otro, otra, otros, otras (another, other)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using otro, otra, otros, otras to say another, other (indefinite adjectives)

temas.regla: In Mexico, recién + preterite means just did: Recién llegué = I just arrived (= Acabo de llegar). Recién + past participle means freshly / newly: recién pintado. Recién never changes; the participle agrees.
temas.titulo: Recién for actions that just happened
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using "recién" with actions that just happened

temas.regla: Más que and menos que compare two things: Mi hermano come más que yo. Más de and menos de go before a number or quantity: Tengo más de cien pesos, menos de la mitad.
temas.titulo: Más que / más de (more than)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Más que/Menos que vs Más de/Menos de (More/Less than)

temas.regla: Cada uno de / cada una de + the, my, these… + plural noun, or + nosotros, ellos, ustedes = each one of. Uno / una matches the gender of the group, and the verb is singular.
temas.titulo: Cada uno / cada una de (each one of)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Cada uno/a de [noun/pronoun] for each one of [something/someone]

temas.regla: Varios / varias = several, some (more than two). It is always plural, agrees with the noun, goes before it with no article (varios amigos), and can stand alone as a pronoun or take de + the group: varios de mis amigos.
temas.titulo: Varios, varias (several, some)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using varios/varias to say some (indefinite adjectives and pronouns)

temas.regla: To agree with a positive statement, use también (me too); with a negative one, use tampoco (me neither). With normal verbs answer with yo, tú, él…; with gustar-type verbs answer with a mí, a ti, a él…
temas.titulo: Me too, me neither: yo también, a mí tampoco
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Yo también/yo tampoco/a mí también/a mí tampoco for me too, me neither

temas.regla: Put an article (el, la, los, las, un, una…) before an adjective and it works as a noun: el rojo = the red one, los jóvenes = young people. The adjective keeps the gender and number of the noun it replaces. Spanish never adds a word for 'one'.
temas.titulo: Adjectives used as nouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish adjectives used as nouns

temas.regla: Cuánto means how much / how many. Before a noun it agrees: cuánto, cuánta, cuántos, cuántas. Before a verb it stays cuánto. It always carries an accent: in direct questions, in exclamations and in indirect questions.
temas.titulo: Cuánto in questions, exclamations and indirect questions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cuánto/-a/-os/-as in interrogative, exclamative and indirect questions

temas.regla: 1,000 is mil (never un mil), and mil never goes plural: dos mil, cien mil. Hundreds before mil agree with a feminine noun (doscientas mil personas). 1,000,000 is un millón, which does go plural (dos millones) and takes de before a noun (un millón de pesos).
temas.titulo: Numbers from 1,000 to 1,000,000
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Numbers from 1,000 to 1,000,000

temas.regla: Aquí and acá mean here (near me). Ahí means there (near you, or not far). Allí and allá mean over there (far from both of us). Acá and allá are vaguer, go well with movement and can take más or muy; in Mexico acá, ahí and allá are the everyday choices.
temas.titulo: Aquí, acá, ahí, allí, allá: here and there
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using aquí, acá, ahí, allí, allá = here and there in Spanish

temas.regla: Both is ambos / ambas (+ plural noun, no article) or los dos / las dos (with the article). Both agree in gender. Los dos is the everyday choice; ambos sounds a little more formal. Both X and Y is tanto X como Y.
temas.titulo: How to say both: ambos, los dos
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "both" in Spanish

temas.regla: To say whether someone is married, single, divorced, engaged or widowed, use estar: estoy casado, está soltera. The adjective agrees with the person, and married to is casado con.
temas.titulo: Estar for relationship status
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar (and not ser) to express relationship statuses

temas.regla: To say what he, she, you (usted), we or they like, use le, nos or les + gusta (one thing or an infinitive) or gustan (several things). The thing liked is the subject; the person is the indirect pronoun.
temas.titulo: Gustar with he, she, we, they
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using gustar to say you like something (he likes, she likes, we like, you like, they like)

temas.regla: Había is the imperfect of hay: there was / there were, used to describe how things were in the past (a scene, a background, a habit). It never changes: había un perro, había muchos perros.
temas.titulo: There was, there were: había
temas.titulo_kwiziq: "There was"/"there were" in Spanish: había

temas.regla: Hubo is the preterite of hay: there was / there were for an event that happened and finished (an accident, a party, a storm, a problem). It never changes: hubo un problema, hubo muchos problemas.
temas.titulo: There was, there were: hubo
temas.titulo_kwiziq: "There was"/"there were": hubo

temas.regla: To say _ago_, use the preterite + **hace** + a length of time: llegué hace un año. Hace always goes before the time, never after.
temas.titulo: Hace for ago
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Use "hace" for "ago" with the preterite tense (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: To talk about people in general (English _one_, _you_, _people_) or to give instructions, use **se** + the verb in the 3rd person singular: aquí se come bien, ¿cómo se dice…? If a plural noun follows, the verb goes plural: se venden casas.
temas.titulo: Impersonal se = one, you, people
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing instructions and general statements in Spanish with the impersonal se = one

temas.regla: In Mexico the preterite is the usual tense for life experiences: ¿alguna vez fuiste a Cancún?, nunca comí chapulines, fui dos veces. The present perfect (¿has ido…?) is also correct, but less common.
temas.titulo: The preterite for experiences
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the preterite tense in Spanish to talk about experiences

temas.regla: In Mexico, todavía no + preterite means _not yet_: todavía no llegó = he hasn't arrived yet. Put todavía no before the verb, or no before the verb and todavía at the end.
temas.titulo: Todavía no with the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using todavía no with El Pretérito Indefinido = not yet (negative expression)

temas.regla: To say how long something has been going on, use the present + desde hace + length of time: surfeo desde hace tres años = I've been surfing for three years. With a starting point, use desde alone: vivo aquí desde 2019.
temas.titulo: Desde hace + present
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using desde (hace) with the present instead of the perfect tense to express since/for

temas.regla: In Mexico the preterite is the default for any finished action, even one from today: hoy desayuné chilaquiles. The present perfect is for a past that's still open, still going on up to now: últimamente he dormido mal, nunca he tenido problemas.
temas.titulo: Present perfect vs preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: When to use the perfect tense versus the simple past (Perfecto vs Indefinido)

temas.regla: To say someone likes doing something, use the pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les) + gusta + infinitive: le gusta surfear, nos gusta bailar. Gusta stays singular, even with several infinitives.
temas.titulo: Gustar + infinitive: he likes, we like, they like
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using gustar to say you like doing something (he likes, she likes, we like, you like, they like)

temas.regla: Use estar, not ser, to say how someone feels: estoy contento, está nerviosa, estamos preocupados. The adjective agrees with the person.
temas.titulo: Estar for feelings and emotions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar (not ser) when talking about feelings and emotions

temas.regla: To say you love a thing or an activity, use encantar, built like gustar: me encanta el mar, me encantan los tacos, me encanta surfear. Keep querer and amar for people.
temas.titulo: To love something or doing something: encantar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "to love something/doing something" in Spanish

temas.regla: Aburrir, molestar, entristecer, preocupar and enojar work like gustar: the thing that causes the feeling is the subject, and the person is me / te / le / nos / les: me aburre el golf, nos molestan los mosquitos.
temas.titulo: Something bores, annoys or saddens you
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "something bores/annoys/saddens you" in Spanish

temas.regla: To describe the physical condition or state that something, someone or a place is in (tired, sick, broken, clean, open, cold...), use estar, not ser.
temas.titulo: Estar for physical condition
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar (not ser) when talking about physical condition of something, someone or a place

temas.regla: To say who something is for, use ser + para + the person: el regalo es para ti. Never estar. After para, use mí and ti, not yo and tú.
temas.titulo: Ser para for a recipient
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ser+preposition para (not estar) to indicate a recipient

temas.regla: To say what something is for, use ser + para + an infinitive or a noun: es para cortar, es para la tabla. Never estar.
temas.titulo: Ser para for a purpose
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ser (not estar) with the preposition para, to indicate a purpose

temas.regla: ¡Qué + noun! means What a...! (¡Qué suerte!); ¡Qué + adjective or adverb! means How...! (¡Qué bonito!, ¡Qué bien!). Qué always has an accent, and there is no article after it.
temas.titulo: Exclamations with qué
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming Spanish exclamatory sentences with qué [noun] or qué [adjective]

temas.regla: Hay que + infinitive means one has to / it's necessary to, said in general, without naming who. It never changes for person; to say who has to, use tener que.
temas.titulo: Hay que for obligation
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Hay que in Spanish (expressing obligation)

temas.regla: Es bueno / es malo (+ infinitive) says something is good or bad for you or of good or bad quality. Está bien / está mal says something is OK, right or correct, or wrong. Bien and mal never change.
temas.titulo: Es bueno/malo vs está bien/mal
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using es bueno/malo or está bien/mal in Spanish

temas.regla: Acabar de + infinitive means to have just done something. Spanish uses the present (acabo de llegar = I've just arrived) where English uses just + past.
temas.titulo: Acabar de + infinitive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Acabar de + [infinitive] = to have just done / just did something in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: When the direct object of a verb like ver, visitar, buscar or conocer is a specific person (or a pet), put a before it: veo a Beto, conozco a Naomi. No a before things or places.
temas.titulo: The personal a
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish personal "a" verbs (ver, visitar, buscar, conocer)

temas.regla: The same is el mismo, la misma, los mismos, las mismas + noun, agreeing with the noun; the same as is el mismo... que. The same thing in general is lo mismo.
temas.titulo: El mismo, la misma = the same
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using definite articles + mismo to say "the same" in Spanish

temas.regla: Sentirse + adjective or adverb says how you feel (me siento bien, se siente sola). Sentir + noun says what you feel (siento frío, siento un dolor). Lo siento = I'm sorry.
temas.titulo: Sentir vs sentirse (to feel)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Sentir vs Sentirse (to feel) in Spanish

temas.regla: When a verb works like a noun (as the subject or the object of another verb), Spanish uses the infinitive, never the gerund: nadar es bueno, me gusta surfear. English _swimming_ is Spanish **nadar**.
temas.titulo: The infinitive as subject or object
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the infinitive (not the gerund) as the subject/object of the verb

temas.regla: To turn a statement into a check like _isn't it?_ or _right?_, add **¿no?** or **¿verdad?** at the end. They never change. After a negative statement, use only **¿verdad?**
temas.titulo: Question tags: ¿no? and ¿verdad?
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to use Spanish question tags: ¿no? ¿verdad?

temas.regla: English often says _I can see, I can hear, I can smell, I can feel_. Spanish usually drops poder and uses the plain present: veo, oigo, huelo, siento. Poder is for real ability or possibility.
temas.titulo: Perception verbs without poder
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish perception verbs: Most verbs of perception usually use the present, not the modal poder

temas.regla: Traer = bring something toward where the speaker is (here). Llevar = take something away to another place (there). Spanish follows the speaker's position strictly, even where English says _bring_.
temas.titulo: Traer vs llevar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verbs Traer vs Llevar (to bring/to take)

temas.regla: For _having_ a drink, use tomar (or beber), never tener. For _having_ food, use comer or the meal verbs desayunar, comer, cenar. Tener means to own or to possess.
temas.titulo: Tomar for having a drink (and comer for food)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the verb tomar for having food/drink

temas.regla: Todavía and aún both mean _still_ (something continues): todavía vivo aquí. With no they mean _not yet_: todavía no / aún no. For _no longer_, use ya no.
temas.titulo: Todavía / aún = still
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using todavía/aún for "still"

temas.regla: Height and length: medir (mido 1.75, mide tres metros de largo). Weight: pesar (peso 70 kilos). Distance: estar a + distance (está a 5 kilómetros). Latin America, Mexico included, uses the metric system.
temas.titulo: Measurements and distances
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Talking about measurements and distances in Spanish

temas.regla: Three words that sound alike: hay (there is / there are, from haber), ahí (there, the place) and ¡ay! (oh! / ouch!). Hay and ay sound the same; ahí has two syllables, stressed on the í.
temas.titulo: Hay, ahí and ay
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between hay, ahí and ay

temas.regla: English _play_ splits in two: jugar for games and sports (jugar fútbol, jugar al ajedrez), tocar for musical instruments and music (tocar la guitarra). Tocar also means _to touch_ and, in me toca, _it's my turn_.
temas.titulo: Jugar vs tocar (to play)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Verbs jugar and tocar: differences

temas.regla: Decades use the plural article los + the number: los ochenta, los (años) noventa, los 2000. The number never takes an -s, and in is en: en los setenta.
temas.titulo: Decades: los noventa
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Talking about decades in Spanish

temas.regla: Most verbs ending in vowel + -cer or vowel + -cir change c to zc in the yo form of the present only: conozco, parezco, traduzco. Every other person is regular: conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocen.
temas.titulo: -cer and -cir verbs: c > zc in yo
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish present tense consonant change c > zc in -cer/-cir verbs

temas.regla: Recordar, acordar and acordarse are o > ue verbs: the o becomes ue in every present form except nosotros (recuerdo, recordamos; me acuerdo, nos acordamos). Recordar algo and acordarse de algo both mean to remember; acordar alone means to agree on.
temas.titulo: Recordar, acordar and acordarse
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate recordar, acordar and acordarse (o > ue) stem-changing -ar verbs in the present tense (El Presente)

temas.regla: To form the preterite of a regular -ar verb, drop -ar and add -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron. The accents on -é and -ó are essential: hablo is I speak, habló is he spoke.
temas.titulo: Regular -ar verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Regular -er and -ir verbs share the same preterite endings: drop -er/-ir and add -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron (comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron).
temas.titulo: -er and -ir verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Ir and ser share the same irregular preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron, with no written accents. Context tells you which verb it is: fui a Ensenada (I went) vs fue un buen día (it was).
temas.titulo: Ir and ser in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate and recognise ir and ser in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Estar is irregular in the preterite: estuve, estuviste, estuvo, estuvimos, estuvieron. The stem is estuv- and none of the forms has a written accent.
temas.titulo: Estar in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate estar in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Hacer is irregular in the preterite: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicieron. The stem is hic-, it becomes hiz- in hizo, and no form has a written accent.
temas.titulo: Hacer in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate hacer in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Dar is an -ar verb, but in the preterite it takes the -er/-ir endings: di, diste, dio, dimos, dieron. Di and dio are one syllable, so they have no written accent.
temas.titulo: Dar in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate dar in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Ver in the preterite is vi, viste, vio, vimos, vieron: regular -er endings on the stem v-, but vi and vio are one syllable and take no written accent.
temas.titulo: Ver in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ver in the preterite tense in Spanish ( El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: To form the imperfect of an -ar verb, drop -ar and add -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban. Every -ar verb is regular in the imperfect, and only nosotros has a written accent.
temas.titulo: -ar verbs in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Regular -er and -ir verbs share one set of imperfect endings: drop -er/-ir and add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían (comía, vivía). Every form carries an accent on the í.
temas.titulo: Regular -er and -ir verbs in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -uir (huir, construir, destruir, incluir…) add a y before the ending in the present: construyo, huyes, incluye, construyen. Nosotros has no y: construimos, huimos.
temas.titulo: Huir and construir in the present
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate huir and construir in present tense in Spanish (El Presente)

temas.regla: Tener is irregular in the preterite: its stem becomes tuv- and it takes endings without accents: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvieron.
temas.titulo: Tener in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate tener in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: In the preterite, leer, creer and proveer change the i to y in él/ella/usted and ellos/ellas/ustedes (leyó, leyeron). The other persons keep the i with an accent: leí, leíste, leímos.
temas.titulo: Leer, creer and proveer in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate leer, creer and proveer in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Poder is irregular in the preterite: stem pud- with unaccented endings: pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudieron. Pude means I managed to; no pude means I tried and failed.
temas.titulo: Poder in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poder in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: In the preterite, -ar verbs ending in -car change c to qu in the yo form only (busqué, saqué, toqué) to keep the hard k sound. All other forms are regular: buscaste, buscó.
temas.titulo: -car verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate-car verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: In the preterite, -ar verbs ending in -gar change g to gu in the yo form only (pagué, llegué, jugué) to keep the hard g sound. All other forms are regular: pagaste, pagó.
temas.titulo: -gar verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate -gar verbs in the Spanish Preterite tense (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: In the preterite, -ar verbs ending in -zar change z to c in the yo form only (empecé, almorcé, crucé), because Spanish writes ce, not ze. All other forms keep the z: empezaste, empezó.
temas.titulo: -zar verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate-zar verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Poner is irregular in the preterite: stem pus- with unaccented endings: puse, pusiste, puso, pusimos, pusieron. Its derivatives (proponer, suponer, componer…) and ponerse follow it.
temas.titulo: Poner in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poner in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: In the preterite, -ir verbs with e in the stem (pedir, servir, repetir, sentir, preferir…) change e to i only in él/ella/usted and ellos/ellas/ustedes: pidió, pidieron. Yo, tú and nosotros stay regular: pedí, pediste, pedimos.
temas.titulo: Stem-changing -ir verbs (e > i) in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate stem-changing-ir verbs (e > i) in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Venir is irregular in the preterite: stem vin- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, with no written accents: vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinieron.
temas.titulo: Venir in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate venir in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Andar is irregular in the preterite: stem anduv- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron: anduve, anduviste, anduvo, anduvimos, anduvieron. Never «andé» or «andó».
temas.titulo: Andar in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate andar in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Use the preterite for actions that happened and finished in the past: at a specific moment, in a closed period, or as a series of events. Markers like ayer, anoche, el lunes, el año pasado and hace dos días call for it.
temas.titulo: The preterite for completed actions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the preterite tense in Spanish for completed actions in the past

temas.regla: Querer is irregular in the preterite: stem quis- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron: quise, quisiste, quiso, quisimos, quisieron. It often means «tried to», and no quiso means «refused».
temas.titulo: Querer in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate querer in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Decir is irregular in the preterite: stem dij- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -eron: dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijeron (no i after the j). Predecir, bendecir, maldecir and contradecir follow it: predijo, bendijo, maldijeron.
temas.titulo: Decir in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate decir in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Oír has regular endings in the preterite, but the i becomes y in él/ella/usted and ellos/ustedes, and the other forms carry an accent: oí, oíste, oyó, oímos, oyeron.
temas.titulo: Oír in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate oír in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Dormir and morir change o to u in él/ella/usted and ellos/ustedes in the preterite: durmió, durmieron; murió, murieron. The other forms are regular: dormí, dormiste, dormimos.
temas.titulo: Dormir and morir in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate dormir and morir in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Traer is irregular in the preterite: stem traj- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -eron: traje, trajiste, trajo, trajimos, trajeron (no i after the j). Atraer, distraer, contraer and extraer follow it.
temas.titulo: Traer in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate traer in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -ducir (conducir, traducir, producir, introducir, reducir) are irregular in the preterite: -duj- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -eron: conduje, condujiste, condujo, condujimos, condujeron.
temas.titulo: -ducir verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate -ducir verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish: introducir, producir, traducir, conducir

temas.regla: Ser is irregular in the imperfect: era, eras, era, éramos, eran. Yo and él/ella share era, and éramos carries an accent.
temas.titulo: Ser in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ser in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Ver is one of only three irregular verbs in the imperfect: it keeps the e of its stem, so it is veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían (never vía).
temas.titulo: Ver in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ver in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Ir is irregular in the imperfect: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban. Only nosotros has an accent (íbamos). It is one of only three irregular verbs in the imperfect, with ser and ver.
temas.titulo: Ir in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ir in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Use the imperfect for things you used to do, or would do, again and again in the past, with no clear start or end. Time words like siempre, todos los días, cada verano, antes or de niño usually go with it.
temas.titulo: The imperfect for past habits
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperfect tense in Spanish to express habits or repeated actions in the past (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Caber and saber share an irregular preterite with a u stem and no accents: cupe, cupiste, cupo, cupimos, cupieron; supe, supiste, supo, supimos, supieron. In the preterite, saber usually means found out.
temas.titulo: Caber and saber in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate caber and saber in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: To describe how things were in the past (time, age, weather, places, people, feelings, what was going on), use the imperfect. It sets the scene; it doesn't tell what happened next.
temas.titulo: The imperfect to describe the past
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperfect tense in Spanish to "describe" a situation in the past

temas.regla: Hacer is regular in the imperfect: hacía, hacías, hacía, hacíamos, hacían. Use it for what you used to do or were doing, and for past weather as background: hacía frío.
temas.titulo: Hacer in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate verb hacer in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Tener is regular in the imperfect: tenía, tenías, tenía, teníamos, tenían. Use it for age, things you had, and states like tener hambre or tener miedo in the past.
temas.titulo: Tener in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate tener in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Pedir changes e to i in the preterite only in the third person: pedí, pediste, pidió, pedimos, pidieron. Yo, tú and nosotros stay regular.
temas.titulo: Pedir in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate stem-changing verb pedir in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -uir (construir, destruir, incluir, contribuir, huir…) take regular -ir preterite endings, but the i becomes y in the third person: construyó, construyeron.
temas.titulo: -uir verbs in the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate -uir verbs in the preterite tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Indefinido)

temas.regla: For most verbs, the affirmative tú command is the same as the él/ella form of the present: habla, come, escribe. Stem changes stay: cierra, vuelve, pide.
temas.titulo: Affirmative tú commands
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the imperative of tú for most verbs (affirmative commands)

temas.regla: Eight common verbs have a short, irregular affirmative tú command: di (decir), haz (hacer), ve (ir), pon (poner), sal (salir), sé (ser), ten (tener), ven (venir).
temas.titulo: Irregular affirmative tú commands
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the imperative of tú for all irregular verbs (irregular affirmative commands)

temas.regla: The present perfect is haber in the present (he, has, ha, hemos, han) + the participle. For -ar verbs, the participle swaps -ar for -ado: hablar → he hablado.
temas.titulo: Regular -ar verbs in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: The present perfect is haber in the present (he, has, ha, hemos, han) + the participle. For -er and -ir verbs, the participle ends in -ido: comer → he comido, vivir → he vivido.
temas.titulo: Regular -er and -ir verbs in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -er, -ir verbs in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: A handful of common verbs have an irregular past participle ending in -to or -cho instead of -ado/-ido: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, roto, vuelto, abierto, muerto, cubierto, resuelto.
temas.titulo: Irregular participles in -to / -cho
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish irregular past participles ending in -to/-cho

temas.regla: Ya + preterite says something has already happened: ya comí = I already ate / I've eaten. In questions it means yet: ¿Ya comiste? = Have you eaten yet? This is the everyday Mexican way to say it.
temas.titulo: Ya with the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ya with the Spanish preterite tense

temas.regla: Ver has an irregular participle, visto. The present perfect is he visto, has visto, ha visto, hemos visto, han visto.
temas.titulo: Ver in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ver in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: Estar is regular in the imperfect: estaba, estabas, estaba, estábamos, estaban. Use it for where someone was and how things were in the past.
temas.titulo: Estar in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate estar in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Some gerunds are irregular: -ir verbs with a stem change use e > i or o > u (pidiendo, durmiendo), and verbs whose stem ends in a vowel use -yendo instead of -iendo (leyendo, oyendo, yendo).
temas.titulo: Irregular gerunds
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming irregular gerunds in Spanish (-ing form)

temas.regla: Estar in the imperfect + gerund (estaba comiendo) describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by another action in the preterite.
temas.titulo: Estaba + gerund
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the progressive imperfect with estar + present participle (El Imperfecto progresivo/continuo)

temas.regla: In verbs ending in consonant + -cer/-cir (vencer, convencer, ejercer, torcer, esparcir), the c becomes z in the yo form of the present to keep the soft sound: venzo, convenzo, ejerzo. The other forms keep the c.
temas.titulo: -cer and -cir verbs: c > z in yo
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish present tense consonant change c>z in -cer/-cir verbs

temas.regla: Hacer in the present perfect is haber in the present + the irregular participle hecho (never hacido). Hecho never changes: he hecho, has hecho, ha hecho, hemos hecho, han hecho.
temas.titulo: Hacer in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate hacer in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: Caber (to fit) is regular in the present except for yo: quepo, cabes, cabe, cabemos, caben. The thing that fits is the subject.
temas.titulo: Caber in the present
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate caber in the present tense in Spanish (El Presente)

temas.regla: Solía, solías, solía, solíamos, solían + infinitive = used to (do something). Soler is regular in the imperfect: no o > ue.
temas.titulo: Soler in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate soler in the imperfect tense (El Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Decir in the present perfect is haber in the present + the irregular participle dicho (never decido): he dicho, has dicho, ha dicho, hemos dicho, han dicho.
temas.titulo: Decir in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate decir in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: Deber is regular in the imperfect: debía, debías, debía, debíamos, debían. Debía + infinitive = was supposed to / had to; debía + noun = owed.
temas.titulo: Deber in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate deber in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Poder is regular in the imperfect, with no o > ue: podía, podías, podía, podíamos, podían. It means could / was able to, as a general ability or possibility in the past.
temas.titulo: Poder in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poder in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Querer is regular in the imperfect, with no e > ie: quería, querías, quería, queríamos, querían. It means wanted (an ongoing wish), and quería is also a polite I'd like.
temas.titulo: Querer in the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate querer in the imperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Poner in the present perfect is haber in the present + the irregular participle puesto (never ponido): he puesto, has puesto, ha puesto, hemos puesto, han puesto. Verbs built on poner do the same: propuesto, compuesto, supuesto.
temas.titulo: Poner in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poner in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: Ser in the present perfect is haber in the present + sido: he sido, has sido, ha sido, hemos sido, han sido. Sido never changes. For been somewhere or a temporary state, use estado (from estar).
temas.titulo: Ser in the present perfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ser in the present perfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Perfecto)

temas.regla: Lo, la, los, las replace a direct object (him, her, it, them, formal you) and match its gender and number. They go before a conjugated verb, or can attach to the end of an infinitive or gerund.
temas.titulo: Direct object pronouns lo, la, los, las
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using lo, la, los, las = him, her, it, them (direct object pronouns)

temas.regla: Me, te and nos are the direct object pronouns for me, you (tú) and us. They go right before the conjugated verb: Te veo mañana. Os is the vosotros form; in Mexico, for ustedes use los / las.
temas.titulo: Direct object pronouns me, te, nos
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using me, te, nos, os = me, you, us, you plural (direct object pronouns)

temas.regla: Le and les mean to / for him, her, it, you (usted / ustedes) or them. They go before the conjugated verb, and Spanish keeps them even when the person is named: Le di el libro a Ana.
temas.titulo: Indirect object pronouns le, les
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using le and les = [to] it, him, her, them (indirect object pronouns)

temas.regla: To / for me, you, him, her, us, them: me, te, le, nos, les (os for vosotros). They go right before the conjugated verb: Mi mamá me manda fotos.
temas.titulo: Indirect object pronouns me, te, le, nos, les
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using me, te, le, nos, os, les (indirect object pronouns)

temas.regla: For this one / these (ones), use este, esta, estos, estas, matching the noun you mean, with no noun after it. For an unknown thing or an idea, use esto, which never changes: ¿Qué es esto?
temas.titulo: Esto, este, esta, estos, estas: this one, these
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using esto, este, esta, estos, estas to say "this", "this one" and "these ones" (demonstrative pronouns)

temas.regla: For that one / those (ones), use ese, esa, esos, esas, matching the noun. Eso (neutral, no plural) is for an unknown thing, an idea or something just said: Eso es mentira.
temas.titulo: Ese, esa, esos, esas, eso: that one, those
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ese, esa, esos, esas, eso for that one, those ones and that (demonstrative pronouns)

temas.regla: For that one / those (ones) far from both speakers, or far back in time, use aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas, matching the noun. Aquello (neutral, no plural) is for an idea or a thing you can't name.
temas.titulo: Aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas: that one over there
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas for that one (over there), those ones (over there) and that (over there) (demonstrative pronouns)

temas.regla: Algo means something, and anything in questions. It never changes form, and an adjective after it is masculine singular: algo rico. In negative sentences use nada instead: no quiero nada.
temas.titulo: Algo: something, anything
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using algo to say something or anything in Spanish

temas.regla: Alguien means someone, and anyone in questions. It is only for people, never changes form and takes a singular verb. As an object it needs the personal a: Busco a alguien. In negative sentences use nadie.
temas.titulo: Alguien: someone, anyone
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using alguien to say someone or anyone in Spanish

temas.regla: Nada means nothing / not anything. After the verb it needs no before the verb: No veo nada (this double negative is correct). At the start of the sentence it stands alone, with no no: Nada me gusta.
temas.titulo: Nada: nothing, not anything
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using nada to say nothing or not anything

temas.regla: Nadie means no one / not anyone. Before the verb it stands alone (Nadie vino); after the verb it needs no before the verb (No vino nadie). As an object it takes the personal a: No conozco a nadie.
temas.titulo: Nadie: no one, nobody, not anyone
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using nadie to say no one, nobody and not anyone

temas.regla: Mucho, poco, demasiado, bastante, suficiente and tanto can stand alone, replacing a noun already mentioned. They agree with that noun: mucho, mucha, muchos, muchas; bastante and suficiente change only for number. Plural masculine on its own (muchos, pocos) can mean many / few people.
temas.titulo: Mucho, poco, demasiado, bastante, suficiente, tanto as pronouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using demasiado, bastante, suficiente, poco, tanto and mucho to express quantity in Spanish (quantitative pronouns)

temas.regla: El mío, la tuya, los suyos, las nuestras replace a possessive + noun (mi tabla → la mía). They agree with the thing owned, not with the owner. After ser the article is usually dropped: es mío.
temas.titulo: Possessive pronouns: el mío, la tuya, el suyo…
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Possessive pronouns in Spanish: mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours and theirs

temas.regla: Alone, todo means everything (singular verb) and todos/todas means everyone or all of them (plural verb). When todo refers to something already mentioned, it agrees with it and usually goes with an object pronoun: me las comí todas.
temas.titulo: Todo = everything, todos = everyone
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using todo to say everything or all (of it) (indefinite pronoun)

temas.regla: Without a noun, alguno / alguna means one, any one (from a known group) and algunos / algunas means some (of them). It agrees with the noun it replaces and is never shortened to algún. For people in general, algunos = some people.
temas.titulo: Alguno, alguna, algunos, algunas as pronouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using alguno, alguna, algunos and algunas to say some, one or any in Spanish (pronouns)

temas.regla: Without a noun, ninguno / ninguna means none, not one, not any (from a known group). It agrees with the noun it replaces, is almost always singular, and is never shortened to ningún. After the verb you need no before it; before the verb you don't.
temas.titulo: Ninguno, ninguna as pronouns (none, not one)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the negative ninguno, ninguna, ningunos and ningunas to say not any (indefinite pronoun)

temas.regla: Without a noun, otro / otra means another one, el otro / la otra means the other one, and otros / otras (los otros, las otras) means others (the others). It agrees with the noun it replaces and never takes un / una.
temas.titulo: Otro, otra, otros, otras as pronouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using otro, otra, otros, otras to say another/another one, other, others (indefinite pronouns)

temas.regla: A number can stand alone, replacing a noun already mentioned: tengo dos. Alone, one is uno or una (never un), 21 is veintiuno or veintiuna, and hundreds agree too: doscientas.
temas.titulo: Numbers as pronouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using numbers as pronouns in Spanish

temas.regla: Mi (no accent) = my, always before a noun. Mí (accent) = me, after a preposition: para mí, a mí, de mí, sin mí. With con it becomes conmigo.
temas.titulo: Mi vs mí
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between mi and mí in Spanish (with or without an accent)

temas.regla: Sé (accent) is a verb: I know (saber) or be! (the tú command of ser). Se (no accent) is a pronoun: se llama, se levanta, aquí se habla español, se lo di.
temas.titulo: Sé vs se
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between sé and se (with and without an accent)

temas.regla: To give a deadline (by Monday, by eight o'clock), use para + a point in time, never por. ¿Para cuándo? = by when? A length of time is not a deadline: en dos semanas, por tres horas.
temas.titulo: Para for a deadline (by…)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using para (not por) for a deadline/time limit

temas.regla: To say where someone or something is headed, use para after verbs of movement (ir, salir, venir, partir) and with vehicles or things going somewhere. Por with a place means through or around, not to.
temas.titulo: Para (not por) for a destination
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using para (not por) for a destination

temas.regla: Before / after something or doing something: antes de, después de, luego de + a noun or an infinitive (antes de la clase, después de comer). The de is required and the verb is never a gerund. Luego de is common in Latin America, a bit more formal.
temas.titulo: Antes de / después de / luego de + noun or infinitive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using antes de /después de/luego de [noun/infinitive] for before/after [something/doing something] (LatAm)

temas.regla: With me is conmigo and with you (tú) is contigo. Every other person uses con + the normal pronoun: con él, con ella, con usted, con nosotros, con ustedes, con ellos.
temas.titulo: Con + pronouns: with me, with you, with him…
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using preposition con followed by a pronoun to say with me, you, him, her, us, you (plural), them

temas.regla: Use por to give the cause or reason behind something: what made it happen (because of, due to, on account of). Para looks forward to a goal; por looks back to a cause.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) for cause or reason
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using por (not para) to express the originating cause or reason

temas.regla: Use por + place for movement through, along, across or by way of a place: caminar por la playa, entrar por la ventana, pasar por Rosarito. Para + place gives the destination instead.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) for through / along a place
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using por (not para) to express "through/along" (a place)

temas.regla: Use por + place to say roughly where something is: around, somewhere near, in the area of (por aquí, por el centro, por ahí). It's vague on purpose; en gives the exact place.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) for an approximate location
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using por (not para) to express approximate location

temas.regla: Para + person gives that person's opinion or point of view: para mí (in my opinion), ¿para ti es caro?, para mi papá… Not por: por mí means I don't mind / fine by me.
temas.titulo: Para mí = in my opinion
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using para (not por) to express opinion

temas.regla: Use para to say who receives something or who an action is meant for: un regalo para ti, cociné para todos. Por + person means because of or on behalf of that person, not for them to receive.
temas.titulo: Para (not por) for the recipient of an action
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using para (not por) to express the recipient of an action

temas.regla: Que links a verb like creer, decir, saber or pensar to the clause that follows (creo que llueve). Unlike English that, it can never be dropped, and it is never pensar de que.
temas.titulo: The conjunction que = that
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the conjunction que to say that

temas.regla: After a preposition (a, para, por, de, en, sin, hacia, sobre…), use mí and ti for I and you. All the other persons keep their usual form: él, ella, usted, nosotros, ustedes, ellos. Exceptions: con (conmigo, contigo) and entre / según (yo, tú).
temas.titulo: Prepositions + pronouns: para mí, sin ti, de él…
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using prepositions a, para, por, de, en, sin, hacia, sobre followed by a pronoun

temas.regla: Porque (because) goes after the main clause; como (since, as) starts the sentence, before the main clause; es que (it's just that, the thing is) introduces an explanation or an excuse, usually in conversation.
temas.titulo: Porque, como and es que (cause)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using porque, como and es que to express cause (subordinate causal clauses)

temas.regla: Pero = but (adds something, even after a negative). Sino = but rather: after a negative, it corrects the first idea and replaces it. Before a conjugated verb, sino becomes sino que.
temas.titulo: Pero, sino and sino que (but)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between pero, sino and sino que in Spanish (but)

temas.regla: To say who your employer or client is, use trabajar para + person or company, never por. Trabajar por means working for money, for a cause, or in someone's place.
temas.titulo: Para to say who you work for
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using para (and not por) to say who you work for

temas.regla: To say how long something lasted, put the time right after the verb with no preposition, or use durante. Por is also common in Mexican speech, especially for planned periods. Never para.
temas.titulo: Duration: durante, por or nothing
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing duration in Spanish with durante/por/no preposition

temas.regla: Most prepositions take mí and ti (para mí, sin ti), but entre and según take the subject pronouns yo and tú: entre tú y yo, según tú. The other pronouns don't change.
temas.titulo: Entre and según + pronouns
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using prepositions entre and según followed by a pronoun

temas.regla: To say from... to... in time or space, use the pair de... a or the pair desde... hasta. Keep the pairs together. Desde... hasta is a bit more emphatic about the start and end points.
temas.titulo: From... to...: de... a and desde... hasta
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using desde/de/hasta/a for from/to in Spanish

temas.regla: Not only... but also = no solo... sino (también) before a noun, adjective or other non-verb; no solo... sino que (también) before a conjugated verb. Never pero también.
temas.titulo: Not only... but also: no solo... sino también
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "not only but" in Spanish

temas.regla: Según means according to. Put it straight before a noun or a pronoun, with no extra preposition: según el pronóstico, según mi mamá. With pronouns it takes yo and tú: según yo, según tú.
temas.titulo: Según = according to
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Preposition "según" in Spanish (according to)

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -or are masculine: el color, el dolor, el error. The main exceptions are la flor and la labor. People and professions in -or add -a for women: el doctor, la doctora.
temas.titulo: Nouns ending in -or are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish nouns ending in -or are masculine

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -ión, -dad, -tad, -umbre, -itis and -sis are feminine (la canción, la ciudad, la costumbre, la crisis), with a few exceptions like el avión, el camión and el análisis. In the plural, -ión loses its accent, and -itis/-sis nouns don't change.
temas.titulo: Nouns in -ión, -dad, -tad, -umbre, -itis, -sis
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender of Spanish nouns ending in -umbre, -ión, -dad, -tad, -itis and -sis and their plural

temas.regla: For words ending in -o or -a, drop the final vowel and add -ito / -ita (plural -itos / -itas): perro → perrito, casa → casita. Words in unstressed -io / -ia drop the whole -io / -ia: despacio → despacito. The new word keeps the gender of the original.
temas.titulo: Diminutive -ito, -ita (words in -o, -a, -io, -ia)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the diminutive suffix -ito, -ita, -itos and -itas with words ending in -o/-a/-io/-ia

temas.regla: -illo / -illa is another diminutive, built like -ito: words in -o / -a take -illo / -illa, words in -e, -n, -r take -cillo, and one-syllable words take -ecillo. In Mexico -ito is the everyday diminutive; -illo lives mostly in words with their own meaning (tortilla, bolsillo, ventanilla).
temas.titulo: Diminutive -illo, -cillo, -ecillo
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the diminutive suffix -illo, -cillo, -ecillo, -ececillo

temas.regla: To say the two / the three…, use los or las + number + noun, in that order; the article agrees with the noun. Los dos / las dos on their own also mean both (of them).
temas.titulo: Plural article + number + noun
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using plural definite article + number + noun

temas.regla: Unos / unas + number + noun means about or approximately. Unos or unas agrees with the noun: unos diez minutos, unas veinte personas. For clock times use como a las… or a eso de las….
temas.titulo: Unos, unas + number = about
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using unos, unas + number = about/approximately

temas.regla: Nouns in -ma that come from Greek are masculine even though they end in -a: el problema, el tema, el sistema, el idioma, el clima. Their plural just adds -s: los problemas. Other -ma nouns are feminine as usual: la cama, la forma.
temas.titulo: Nouns ending in -ma (Greek origin)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender and plural of Spanish nouns ending in -ma (Greek origin)

temas.regla: Some nouns for people form the feminine with a special ending: -esa (alcaldesa, princesa), -triz (actriz, emperatriz), -ina (heroína, reina) or -isa (poetisa, sacerdotisa). They are feminine and form the plural normally, except -triz → -trices.
temas.titulo: Feminine nouns in -esa, -triz, -ina, -isa
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender and plural of Spanish nouns ending in -esa, -triz, -ina, -isa
