temas.regla: Some nouns ending in -o are feminine because they are short forms of feminine nouns: la foto (fotografía), la moto (motocicleta), la radio (radiodifusión), la disco (discoteca). They keep the feminine article and adjectives, and the plural adds -s.
temas.titulo: Feminine nouns in -o (shortened words)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Some Spanish nouns ending in -o (shortened from a feminine noun) are feminine

temas.regla: Some nouns are plural in English but singular in Spanish (people → la gente, clothes → la ropa, police → la policía), and some are singular in English but usually plural in Spanish (news → las noticias, furniture → los muebles, advice → los consejos). The verb and adjectives follow the Spanish noun.
temas.titulo: Plural in English, singular in Spanish (and vice versa)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Nouns that are plural in English but singular in Spanish, and vice versa (collective nouns)

temas.regla: To talk about a family by its surname, use los + the surname unchanged: los García, los Hernández, los Simpson. The article and the verb go plural, the surname doesn't.
temas.titulo: Surnames don't go plural
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Surnames in Spanish don't turn into plurals

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -ía or -ia are almost always feminine: la farmacia, la historia, la panadería. The big exception is el día; and el / la policía, el / la guía change meaning or follow the person. Plural: add -s.
temas.titulo: Most nouns in -ía / -ia are feminine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Most Spanish nouns ending in -ía/-ia are feminine

temas.regla: No goes in front of the whole verb group: before the conjugated verb (no he comido, no voy a ir, no puedo salir, no estoy trabajando) and before any pronoun in front of it (no lo he visto). For a plain negative it never goes in the middle.
temas.titulo: Negation with no in compound verb forms
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming negative sentences using no (negation) with complex verbal structures

temas.regla: Cómo (how), dónde (where) and cuándo (when) always take an accent in direct questions, indirect questions (no sé dónde…, dime cuándo…) and exclamations (¡cómo llueve!). With no question or exclamation, they're como, donde, cuando.
temas.titulo: Cómo, dónde, cuándo in questions and exclamations
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cómo, dónde and cuándo in interrogative, exclamatory and indirect sentences

temas.regla: Por qué (two words, accent) = why, in direct and indirect questions: ¿Por qué lloras? No sé por qué. Porque (one word, no accent) = because: Lloro porque estoy feliz.
temas.titulo: Porque vs por qué
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between porque and por qué in Spanish (because and why)

temas.regla: Cuánto + noun asks how much / how many and agrees with the noun: cuánto, cuánta, cuántos, cuántas. Singular for things you can't count, plural for things you can. Always with an accent.
temas.titulo: Cuánto + noun: how much, how many
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cuánto + noun to ask how much/how many in Spanish (interrogative adjective)

temas.regla: Right before a verb, ¿cuánto…? means how much and never changes: ¿cuánto cuesta?, ¿cuánto cuestan?, ¿cuánto pesas? Only when it stands for a noun already mentioned does it agree: ¿cuántas quieres?
temas.titulo: Cuánto + verb: how much
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Cuánto + verb in interrogative sentences

temas.regla: Add with más, subtract with menos, multiply with por, divide with entre (or dividido entre). The result comes after son, or es igual a; with uno, use es.
temas.titulo: Doing arithmetic: más, menos, por, entre
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Doing arithmetic in Spanish (numbers, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division)

temas.regla: Primero, segundo, tercero, cuarto, quinto, sexto, séptimo, octavo, noveno, décimo. They agree with the noun and usually go before it; primero and tercero become primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun.
temas.titulo: Ordinal numbers: first to tenth
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming ordinal numbers in Spanish (1st, 2nd, 10th...)

temas.regla: Hundreds agree with the noun (doscientos pesos, doscientas personas); mil never changes and never takes un; millón takes un, has a plural (millones) and needs de before a noun. Un billón is a million millions: English billion is mil millones.
temas.titulo: Big numbers: hundreds, thousands, millions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing large numbers in Spanish: hundreds, thousands, millions and billions

temas.regla: Centuries are written with Roman numerals after siglo (el siglo XXI) and read as ordinary cardinal numbers: el siglo veintiuno, el siglo quince. From I to X you'll also hear ordinals: el siglo primero, el siglo quinto.
temas.titulo: Centuries with Roman numerals
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to express centuries in Spanish with Roman numerals

temas.regla: Say percentages as el + number + por ciento (+ de + noun): el veinte por ciento de los clientes. Un also works and often sounds approximate; cien por ciento means 100 % or totally. Por ciento is two words and never takes -s.
temas.titulo: Percentages: el diez por ciento
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to talk about percentages in Spanish

temas.regla: Adjectives ending in -ar have one singular form for masculine and feminine and add -es for the plural: popular → populares.
temas.titulo: Forming singular and plural of adjectives ending in -ar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming singular and plural of Spanish adjectives ending in -ar

temas.regla: Tampoco = either / neither. Before the verb it goes alone (tampoco viene); after the verb, it needs no before the verb (no viene tampoco).
temas.titulo: Using tampoco for either / neither
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using tampoco for either/neither in Spanish

temas.regla: Superlative: el / la / los / las + más / menos + adjective, agreeing with the noun. In or of = de: el más alto de la clase.
temas.titulo: How to say the most / the least + adjective (superlatives)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say the most / the least + adjective in Spanish (superlatives)

temas.regla: Irregular superlatives: el / la mejor (best), peor (worst), mayor (oldest, biggest), menor (youngest, smallest); plural -es. Never más mejor.
temas.titulo: How to say the best, the worst, the oldest, the youngest (irregular superlatives)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say the best/the worst/the oldest/the youngest in Spanish (irregular superlatives)

temas.regla: Before a masculine singular noun, bueno → buen and malo → mal. Grande → gran before any singular noun, and it means great. Plurals don't shorten.
temas.titulo: Bueno, malo, grande become buen, mal, gran before a noun
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Bueno, malo, grande become buen, mal, gran before a noun (apócope)

temas.regla: Primero → primer and tercero → tercer only before a masculine singular noun. Feminine, plural or without a noun: full form.
temas.titulo: Primero and tercero become primer and tercer before a noun
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Primero and tercero become primer and tercer before a noun (Spanish apócope)

temas.regla: -ísimo means extremely: drop the final vowel (caro → carísimo), drop -io (limpio → limpísimo), or just add it after -l and -ar (fácil → facilísimo, popular → popularísimo).
temas.titulo: Superlatives with -ísimo: adjectives ending in a vowel, -io, -l and -ar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish superlatives -ísimo with adjectives ending in a single vowel, -io, -l and -ar

temas.regla: -ísimo with spelling changes: -co → -quísimo, -go → -guísimo, -ble → -bilísimo, -z → -císimo, and -or / -n add -císimo.
temas.titulo: Superlatives with -ísimo: adjectives ending in -co, -go, -ble, -z, -or and -n
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish superlatives -ísimo with adjectives ending in -co, -go, -ble,-z, -or and -n

temas.regla: Junto, junta, juntos, juntas (together) agree with the noun. Mixed groups use juntos. Singular junto / junta goes with uncountable nouns: piled up.
temas.titulo: Using junto, junta, juntos and juntas = together
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using junto, junta, juntos and juntas = together in Spanish

temas.regla: A past participle (-ado, -ido) can work as an adjective and then agrees in gender and number: cansado, cansada, cansados, cansadas.
temas.titulo: Past participles as adjectives
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish past participles as adjectives

temas.regla: Poco = little, not much (negative); un poco = a bit (positive). With nouns: poco / poca / pocos / pocas agree; un poco de + uncountable noun.
temas.titulo: Difference between poco and un poco
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between "poco" and "un poco" in Spanish

temas.regla: Igual de + adjective / adverb + que = as … as. Igual de never changes; the adjective agrees. With a plural subject comparing each other, drop que.
temas.titulo: Igual de … que = as … as
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Igual de ... que = as ... as in Spanish (comparatives with adjectives and adverbs)

temas.regla: Long possessives go after the noun and agree with the thing owned: mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro (-a, -os, -as). Un amigo mío = a friend of mine.
temas.titulo: Long-form possessive adjectives: mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish long-form possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their)

temas.regla: Unos cuantos / unas cuantas + plural noun = a few. Always plural, and it agrees in gender with the noun.
temas.titulo: Using unos cuantos / unas cuantas + noun for a few
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using unos cuantos/unas cuantas + noun for "a few" (quantitative adjectives)

temas.regla: To contrast with what someone said: after a negative, yo sí; after an affirmative, yo no. With verbs like gustar: a mí sí / a mí no.
temas.titulo: Using yo sí / yo no / a mí sí / a mí no for contrasting answers
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using yo sí/yo no/a mí sí/a mí no (I do/I don't): Spanish contrasting answers

temas.regla: Cierto before a noun = a certain (no un): cierta persona. It agrees. After the noun it means true: una noticia cierta.
temas.titulo: Using cierto, cierta, ciertos, ciertas for certain
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cierto, cierta, ciertos, ciertas for certain in Spanish (indefinite adjectives)

temas.regla: Bien before an adjective or adverb means very: bien rico, bien tarde. Bien never changes; the adjective agrees. Bien mal = very bad.
temas.titulo: Using bien as an intensifier (very)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish adverb bien as an intensifier (very)

temas.regla: Alguno / alguna / algunos / algunas + de + noun or pronoun = one of / some of. Singular = one (not specific); plural = some.
temas.titulo: Alguno / alguna / algunos / algunas de for one of, some of
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Alguno/-a/-os/-as de for "one/some of" (partitives)

temas.regla: Cuánto (with accent) asks or exclaims how much / how many, also in indirect questions. Cuanto (no accent) is relative: cuanto antes, en cuanto, cuanto más.
temas.titulo: Difference between cuánto and cuanto (with and without accent)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between cuánto and cuanto in Spanish (with and without accent)

temas.regla: Apenas goes alone before the verb, or after it with no in front. Casi always takes no, in that order: casi no.
temas.titulo: Using apenas / casi no for _hardly_
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using apenas/casi for hardly in Spanish

temas.regla: Nunca before the verb goes alone (nunca como); after the verb it needs no before the verb (no como nunca). Pronouns stay attached to the verb.
temas.titulo: Using nunca in negative sentences
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using nunca in Spanish negative sentences

temas.regla: Ni… ni… = neither… nor, before each element. Before the verb: no extra no. After the verb: no before the verb (no vino ni Beto ni Lucas).
temas.titulo: Using ni… ni… for neither… nor…
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ni... ni... for neither... nor... in Spanish

temas.regla: Que (who/that/which) works for people and things and never changes. Quien / quienes = who, for people only. El cual / la cual / los cuales / las cuales agree in gender and number. Quien and el cual are more formal than que.
temas.titulo: Que / el cual / quien = who, that, which (relative pronouns)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Que/ el cual/ la cual/ los cuales/ quien/ quienes = who, that, which (Spanish relative pronouns)

temas.regla: When le or les (to him/her/them) comes before lo, la, los or las (it/them), it becomes se: se lo di (not le lo di). Indirect pronoun first, direct second.
temas.titulo: Le / les become se before lo, la, los, las
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish pronouns le / les become se when used with lo, la, los, las (indirect with direct pronouns)

temas.regla: Lo que = what / the thing that, for an idea, not a specific noun: Lo que quiero es descansar. After a comma it means which, referring to the whole previous idea. All that = todo lo que, never todo que.
temas.titulo: Using lo que = what, which, the thing that
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using lo que = what, which, that which, the thing that (Spanish relative pronouns)

temas.regla: With a conjugated verb (any tense) and with negative commands, object and reflexive pronouns go in front of the verb, as separate words: lo compré, no lo toques. Order: reflexive, then indirect, then direct (se me, me lo).
temas.titulo: Position of pronouns with conjugated verbs
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Position of pronouns with conjugated verbs in Spanish

temas.regla: With a conjugated verb + infinitive or gerund, pronouns go either in front of the whole phrase or attached to the end of the infinitive/gerund (la voy a escribir = voy a escribirla), never in the middle. With affirmative commands they must be attached: dámelo.
temas.titulo: Pronouns with infinitives, gerunds and affirmative commands
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Position of Spanish direct and indirect object pronouns with infinitive/present participle and affirmative commands

temas.regla: Reciprocal verbs (each other) use the plural reflexive pronouns nos and se: nos queremos, se ayudan. The pronoun follows the usual position rules. Add el uno al otro or mutuamente to stress it.
temas.titulo: Reciprocal verbs and the position of the pronoun
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Reciprocal verbs in Spanish and position of the reflexive pronoun

temas.regla: With gustar-type verbs, the short pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les) is required. The a + pronoun or a + person (a mí, a María) is optional and adds emphasis or clarity, but can never replace the short pronoun.
temas.titulo: Repeating the indirect pronoun with verbs like gustar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Repetition of indirect object pronouns in Spanish with verbs like gustar

temas.regla: Quién / quiénes (accent) asks a question, direct or indirect: ¿Quién viene? No sé quién viene. Quien / quienes (no accent) is a relative: mi tío, quien vive aquí; quien estudia aprueba.
temas.titulo: Quién vs quien (with and without an accent)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between quién and quien in Spanish (with and without an accent)

temas.regla: Costar = to cost (money): cuesta 200 pesos; add an indirect pronoun to say who paid: nos costó. Me cuesta + infinitive = I find it hard to: me cuesta madrugar. It works like gustar.
temas.titulo: Costar vs costar a alguien algo
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verb Costar vs Costar a alguien algo

temas.regla: Haber in the imperfect (había, habías, había, habíamos, habían) + past participle: había surfeado.
temas.titulo: Conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the pluperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar, -er, and -ir verbs in the pluperfect tense in Spanish (El Pluscuamperfecto de Indicativo)

temas.regla: Haber in the imperfect + an irregular participle: hecho, escrito, visto, dicho, puesto.
temas.titulo: Conjugate hacer, escribir, ver, decir and poner in the pluperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate hacer, escribir, ver, decir, poner in the pluperfect tense in Spanish (El Pluscuamperfecto)

temas.regla: Ya (already) goes before haber or after the participle, never between them: ya había comido / había comido ya.
temas.titulo: Using ya with the pluperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ya with the pluperfect tense in Spanish (El Pretérito Pluscuamperfecto)

temas.regla: Take the present-tense yo form, drop the -o and add -e, -es, -e, -emos, -en. -ar verbs switch to e.
temas.titulo: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Take the present-tense yo form, drop the -o and add -a, -as, -a, -amos, -an. -er and -ir verbs switch to a.
temas.titulo: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Ir has the irregular stem vay- with regular endings: vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate irregular verb ir in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb ir in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Ser has the irregular stem se- with regular endings: sea, seas, sea, seamos, sean.
temas.titulo: Conjugate ser in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ser in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: If the present-tense yo form ends in -go, the g stays through the whole subjunctive, with -er / -ir endings: tenga, tengas, tengamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate yo-go verbs in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate yo-go verbs in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Querer que + present subjunctive when the subjects are different; same subject: querer + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Querer que + the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Querer que followed by the Spanish present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Infinitive + -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án. The same endings for -ar, -er and -ir verbs.
temas.titulo: Conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Tener has the irregular future stem tendr- with the regular endings: tendré, tendrás, tendrá, tendremos, tendrán.
temas.titulo: Conjugate tener in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate tener in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple)

temas.regla: Decir has the irregular future stem dir- with the regular endings: diré, dirás, dirá, diremos, dirán.
temas.titulo: Conjugate decir in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb decir in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Salir has the irregular future stem saldr- with the regular endings: saldré, saldrás, saldrá, saldremos, saldrán.
temas.titulo: Conjugate salir in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb salir in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Cuando + subjunctive for a future event that hasn't happened yet; cuando + indicative for what really happens, like habits.
temas.titulo: Cuando + the present subjunctive vs cuando + the present indicative
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Cuando + the present subjunctive vs Cuando + the present indicative in Spanish

temas.regla: The simple future expresses what will happen, what probably will happen, and predictions: estarán ocupados; habrá coches voladores.
temas.titulo: Using the simple future for probability and predictions in the future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish simple future to express probabilities or predictions in the future (El Futuro Simple)

temas.regla: To guess or speculate about what is probably true right now, use the simple future: ¿Dónde estará Beto? Estará en el agua.
temas.titulo: Using the simple future to guess about the present
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the simple future in Spanish for prediction, speculation and probability in the present (El Futuro Simple)

temas.regla: In affirmative commands with reflexive verbs, the pronoun goes after the verb, attached to it. With nosotros, the final s drops: levantémonos.
temas.titulo: Using the imperative with reflexive pronouns: affirmative commands
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperative with reflexive pronouns: affirmative commands (El Imperativo)

temas.regla: Poder drops the e of its infinitive to make the stem podr-, then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate poder in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb poder in the future tense in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Querer drops the e of its infinitive to make the stem querr- (with double r), then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate querer in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb querer in the future tense in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Hacer uses the irregular stem har-, then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate hacer in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb hacer in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Poner replaces the e of its infinitive with d to make the stem pondr-, then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate poner in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poner in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Caber and saber drop the e of the infinitive to make the stems cabr- and sabr-, then add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate caber and saber in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verbs caber and saber in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Valer replaces the e of its infinitive with d to make the stem valdr-, then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate valer in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate valer in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Venir replaces the i of its infinitive with d to make the stem vendr-, then adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án.
temas.titulo: Conjugate venir in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb venir in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the whole infinitive. The same endings for -ar, -er and -ir verbs.
temas.titulo: Conjugate regular verbs in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate regular verbs in the conditional in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Hacer has the irregular stem har- in the conditional, with the regular endings: haría, harías, haría, haríamos, harían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate hacer in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate hacer in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Tener has the irregular stem tendr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: tendría, tendrías, tendría, tendríamos, tendrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate tener in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate tener in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Poder has the irregular stem podr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: podría, podrías, podría, podríamos, podrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate poder in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poder in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Querer has the irregular stem querr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: querría, querrías, querría, querríamos, querrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate querer in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate verb querer in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Poner has the irregular stem pondr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: pondría, pondrías, pondría, pondríamos, pondrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate poner in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poner in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Decir has the irregular stem dir- in the conditional, with the regular endings: diría, dirías, diría, diríamos, dirían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate decir in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate decir in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Salir has the irregular stem saldr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: saldría, saldrías, saldría, saldríamos, saldrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate salir in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate salir in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Valer has the irregular stem valdr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: valdría, valdrías, valdría, valdríamos, valdrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate valer in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate valer in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -car change c to qu in every form of the present subjunctive: busque, busques, busquemos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -car verbs (c > qu) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem-changing -car verbs (c > qu) in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -gar change g to gu in every form of the present subjunctive: pague, pagues, paguemos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -gar verbs (g > gu) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish -gar verbs: g > gu in all forms in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -zar change z to c in every form of the present subjunctive: utilice, utilices, utilicemos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -zar verbs (z > c) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verbs ending in -zar change z > c in all forms in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Venir has the irregular stem vendr- in the conditional, with the regular endings: vendría, vendrías, vendría, vendríamos, vendrían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate venir in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate venir in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Estar has a regular stem and endings in the present subjunctive, with a written accent on the last syllable except estemos: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estén.
temas.titulo: Conjugate estar in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular estar in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Dar has the short stem d- with regular endings: dé, des, dé, demos, den. Dé carries an accent to tell it apart from de.
temas.titulo: Conjugate dar in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb dar in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Saber has the irregular stem sep- with regular endings: sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate saber in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb saber in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Verbs with e > i in the present keep the i in every form of the present subjunctive, nosotros included: pida, pidamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate e > i verbs in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate e > i verbs in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: -ar verbs with o > ue in the present keep it in the subjunctive, except nosotros: sueñe, sueñes, soñemos, sueñen.
temas.titulo: Conjugate stem-changing -ar verbs (o > ue) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem-changing -ar verbs (o > ue) in the present subjunctive (El Presente Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: -er verbs with o > ue in the present keep it in the subjunctive, except nosotros: vuelva, vuelvas, volvamos, vuelvan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate stem-changing -er verbs (o > ue) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem-changing -er verbs: (o > ue) in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Dormir and morir change o > ue in the subjunctive, and in nosotros o > u: duerma, duermas, durmamos, duerman.
temas.titulo: Conjugate dormir and morir in the present subjunctive (o > u in nosotros)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate stem-changing verbs: o > u (1st person plural) in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -ger and -gir change g to j in every form of the present subjunctive: proteja, dirija, escojamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -ger and -gir verbs (g > j) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish -ger and -gir verbs: g > j in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: To say should, use deber in the conditional + infinitive: debería, deberías, debería, deberíamos, deberían + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Using deber to say should
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using deber to say should in Spanish

temas.regla: Tener que in the conditional uses the stem tendr-: tendría, tendrías, tendría, tendríamos, tendrían + que + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Conjugate tener que (would have to) in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate tener que (would have to) in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Caber and saber have irregular conditional stems cabr- and sabr-, with regular endings: cabría, sabría, cabríamos, sabríamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate caber and saber in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular -er verbs caber and saber in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Verbs ending in -uir add a y between the stem and the ending in every form of the present subjunctive: huya, construya, construyamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -uir verbs in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish -uir verbs in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Haber has the future stem habr-: habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habrán. Habrá alone means there will be.
temas.titulo: Conjugate haber in the simple future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate irregular verb haber in the simple future in Spanish (El Futuro Simple/Imperfecto)

temas.regla: Haber has the conditional stem habr-: habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían. Habría alone means there would be and stays singular.
temas.titulo: Conjugate haber in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate haber in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Empezar and comenzar change z to c in every form and e to ie in every form except nosotros: empiece, empecemos, empiecen.
temas.titulo: Conjugate empezar and comenzar in the present subjunctive (z > c and e > ie)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Some Spanish -zar verbs change z > c and e > ie in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Aún no / todavía no + pluperfect says something hadn't happened yet when another past event happened (preterite): todavía no había comido cuando llegaste.
temas.titulo: Using aún no / todavía no with the pluperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using aún no/todavía no with the pluperfect in Spanish (El Pretérito Pluscuamperfecto)

temas.regla: Estar in the preterite (estuve, estuviste, estuvo, estuvimos, estuvieron) + gerund (-ando, -iendo): estuve trabajando.
temas.titulo: Forming the preterite progressive with estar + gerund
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the progressive preterite tense in Spanish with estar + present participle (El Indefinido Progresivo)

temas.regla: Deber is regular in the conditional: debería, deberías, debería, deberíamos, deberían, always followed by an infinitive.
temas.titulo: Conjugate deber in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate deber in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Verbs in vowel + -cer / -cir that have zc in the yo present keep zc in every form of the present subjunctive: conozca, produzcamos.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -cer and -cir verbs (c > zc) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish -cer/-cir verbs (c>zc) in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Poder changes o > ue in the present subjunctive except in nosotros: pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, puedan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate poder in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate poder [o > ue] in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: -ar verbs with e > ie in the present keep it in the subjunctive except nosotros: cierre, cierres, cerremos, cierren.
temas.titulo: Conjugate stem-changing -ar verbs (e > ie) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate stem changing -ar verbs (e > ie) in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: -er verbs with e > ie in the present keep it in the subjunctive except nosotros: entienda, pierdas, entendamos, enciendan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate stem-changing -er verbs (e > ie) in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem changing -er verbs (e > ie) in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Querer changes e > ie in the present subjunctive except in nosotros: quiera, quieras, quiera, queramos, quieran.
temas.titulo: Conjugate querer in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem-changing verb querer (e > ie) in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Negative tú commands use the tú form of the present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no digas. Pronouns go before the verb.
temas.titulo: Forming negative tú commands
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the Spanish imperative of tú (negative commands)

temas.regla: Commands for usted, ustedes and nosotros, affirmative and negative, use the present subjunctive: hable, coman, comamos, no comamos.
temas.titulo: Forming commands for usted, ustedes and nosotros
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the imperative for usted/ustedes/nosotros/nosotras (affirmative and negative commands)

temas.regla: -ir verbs with e > ie change e > ie in the subjunctive, and e > i in nosotros: sienta, sientas, sintamos, sientan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -ir verbs with e > ie in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Stem-changing verbs in Spanish: -ir verbs with e > ie change in the present subjunctive (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Seguir and its family change e > i and gu > g in every form of the present subjunctive: siga, sigas, sigamos, consigan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate seguir, conseguir and perseguir in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate Spanish stem-changing verbs (e > i) and (gu > g): seguir, conseguir, perseguir in the present subjunctive (El Presente Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Haber has the stem hay- in the present subjunctive: haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayan. Alone, only haya is used (the subjunctive of hay).
temas.titulo: Conjugate haber in the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate haber in the present subjunctive in Spanish (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Estar in the present perfect (he estado, has estado, ha estado, hemos estado, han estado) + gerund (-ando, -iendo): he estado trabajando.
temas.titulo: Forming the present perfect progressive with estar + gerund
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the present perfect progressive tense in Spanish with estar + present participle (El Pretérito Perfecto Progresivo)

temas.regla: Estar in the pluperfect (había estado, habías estado, había estado, habíamos estado, habían estado) + gerund (-ando, -iendo): había estado trabajando.
temas.titulo: Forming the pluperfect progressive with estar + gerund
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the pluperfect progressive tense in Spanish with estar + present participle (El Pluscuamperfecto Progresivo)

temas.regla: Ser is regular in the conditional: sería, serías, sería, seríamos, serían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate ser in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate ser in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Estar is regular in the conditional: estaría, estarías, estaría, estaríamos, estarían.
temas.titulo: Conjugate estar in the conditional
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Conjugate estar in the conditional tense in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Verbs in -uar like actuar and continuar take an accent on the u in the present except nosotros: actúo, actúas, actúa, actuamos, actúan.
temas.titulo: Conjugate -uar verbs in the present: actuar, continuar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish -uar verbs in the present tense (El Presente: actuar, continuar)

temas.regla: Some -iar verbs (enviar, criar, fotografiar) take an accent on the i in the present except nosotros: envío, envías, envía, enviamos, envían.
temas.titulo: Some -iar verbs take an accent in the present: enviar, criar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Some Spanish -iar verbs in the present tense take an accent (liar, enviar, criar)

temas.regla: In affirmative commands, the indirect pronoun comes first, then the direct one, both attached to the verb: dámelo. Le / les become se: pídeselo.
temas.titulo: Using double pronouns with the imperative
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using double pronouns with the imperative in Spanish (El Imperativo)

temas.regla: Estar in the simple future (estaré, estarás, estará, estaremos, estarán) + gerund (-ando, -iendo): estaré trabajando.
temas.titulo: Forming the future progressive with estar + gerund
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the progressive future tense in Spanish with estar + present participle (El Futuro Progresivo)

temas.regla: Use the pluperfect for the earlier of two past actions (the past of the past): había llegado cuando llamaste.
temas.titulo: Using the pluperfect for a past action before another past action
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the pluperfect tense to indicate that a past action happens before another past action (El Pluscuamperfecto)

temas.regla: Esperar que + present subjunctive expresses hope about something that happens or will happen. Same subject: esperar + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Using esperar que + present subjunctive to express hope
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using esperar que + present subjunctive in Spanish to express hope

temas.regla: Ojalá (or ojalá que) + present subjunctive = I hope, hopefully, about the future. Never the indicative. It's stronger than espero que.
temas.titulo: Using ojalá + the present subjunctive to express hope
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ojalá + the present subjunctive to express hope (El Presente de Subjuntivo)

temas.regla: Mientras + present indicative = while (two things at the same time). Mientras + present subjunctive = as long as (a condition).
temas.titulo: Mientras with the present indicative or the present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Mientras with the present indicative or the present subjunctive in Spanish

temas.regla: Saber: facts, info (saber que, si, dónde…) and skills (saber + infinitive). Conocer: being familiar with people, places and things; with people it takes a.
temas.titulo: Difference between saber and conocer (to know)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between Spanish verbs saber and conocer (to know)

temas.regla: Tal vez, quizás, quizá (maybe) take the indicative or the subjunctive. Present or future doubt: present indicative or subjunctive. At the end of the sentence: only indicative.
temas.titulo: Subjunctive or indicative after tal vez and quizás
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the subjunctive or the indicative after tal vez and quizás to express doubt in Spanish

temas.regla: To say who something belongs to: thing + ser + de + person. Never estar: la tabla es de Beto.
temas.titulo: Ser de (not estar) to indicate ownership
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using ser de (not estar) to indicate ownership

temas.regla: For a temporary job, use estar de + job (no article): estoy de mesero. For a permanent profession, use ser: soy cerrajero.
temas.titulo: Estar de (not ser) for a temporary job
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar (not ser) + de for a temporary job

temas.regla: For prices and quantities that fluctuate, use estar + a: el kilo de aguacate está a 60 pesos; el dólar estaba a 20 pesos.
temas.titulo: Estar a (not ser) for fluctuating prices and quantities
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Using estar (not ser) + preposition a with fluctuating quantities and prices

temas.regla: Material: ser de + material, or estar hecho de + material (hecho agrees: hecha, hechos, hechas). Question: ¿De qué es? / ¿De qué está hecho?
temas.titulo: Estar hecho de or ser de to say what something is made of
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using estar hecho de or ser de to indicate what something is made of in Spanish

temas.regla: Ir in the imperfect (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban) + a + infinitive = was / were going to: plans, things about to happen.
temas.titulo: Using ir in the imperfect to say was / were going to
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ir in the imperfect tense in Spanish to express was/were going to [do something]

temas.regla: An action in progress (cuando + imperfect) is interrupted by a new action (preterite): cuando me bañaba, sonó el teléfono.
temas.titulo: The preterite combined with cuando + the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish preterite tense combined with cuando + the Spanish imperfect tense

temas.regla: The present can refer to the future when a time phrase says so: el año que viene viajo; mañana vamos a la playa. Without it, it's the present.
temas.titulo: Using the present to refer to a future action (with a future time phrase)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the present tense in Spanish in order to refer to a future action (only future time indications)

temas.regla: Passive se: se + verb in the 3rd person, singular or plural to agree with the thing: se vende carro, se venden carros.
temas.titulo: Forming the passive with se (la pasiva refleja)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the Spanish passive with se (la pasiva refleja)

temas.regla: For a likely condition: si + present, then present or future. Never si + present subjunctive or si + future.
temas.titulo: Si + present indicative, then present or future
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Si [if] followed by present indicative + main clause (present tense/future tense)

temas.regla: Si + present, then a command: affirmative imperative (dile) or negative with the subjunctive (no manejes). Advice can also use debería / tendrías que.
temas.titulo: Si + present indicative, then a command, request or advice
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Si [if] followed by present indicative + main clause [command/request/advice]

temas.regla: Dejar (conjugated) + de + infinitive = to stop doing, to give up doing: dejé de fumar. Never a gerund after de.
temas.titulo: Dejar de + infinitive: to stop doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using dejar de + [infinitive] = to stop doing something/to give up something

temas.regla: Hace + length of time + que + present = have been doing for: hace un mes que estudio. It goes at the start, and never with the present perfect.
temas.titulo: Hace + time + que + present: how long you've been doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Hace + length of time + que + present tense in Spanish to say how long one has done something

temas.regla: To say by + -ing, use the gerund alone (-ando, -iendo), with no preposition: aprendo repitiendo, never por repitiendo.
temas.titulo: Using the gerund to say by doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the gerund in Spanish to say by [doing something]

temas.regla: Estar (conjugated) + a punto de + infinitive = to be about to. In the present perfect it can mean it nearly happened but didn't.
temas.titulo: Estar a punto de + infinitive: to be about to do something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Estar a punto de + [infinitive] = to be about to do something in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: To end up doing: acabar / terminar + por + infinitive, or acabar / terminar + gerund (no preposition). Same meaning.
temas.titulo: Acabar / terminar + por infinitive or + gerund: to end up doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using acabar/terminar + [infinitive/present participle] = to end up doing something in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: Volver (conjugated) + a + infinitive = to do again: volví a llamarla. In the present it often refers to the future.
temas.titulo: Volver a + infinitive to say again
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using volver a + [infinitive] to express repetition of an action in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: Poder in the conditional + infinitive: polite requests (¿podría pasarme…?) and suggestions about what someone could do (podrías llamarla).
temas.titulo: Using podría to make polite requests and suggestions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using poder to say could [do something] for polite requests and suggestions in Spanish (El Condicional Simple)

temas.regla: Se + puede / pueden or debe / deben + infinitive = you can / you must, in general. The verb agrees with the thing: se deben pagar impuestos.
temas.titulo: The passive se with deber and poder
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the Spanish passive se with modal verbs deber/poder (la pasiva refleja)

temas.regla: Time markers of frequency or ongoing time (siempre, todos los días, cada mes, de niño) → imperfect. Specific, closed times (ayer, el año pasado, una vez) → preterite.
temas.titulo: The imperfect vs the preterite: time markers
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperfect vs the preterite in Spanish (time markers)

temas.regla: There was / were: había (imperfect) describes a scene; hubo (preterite) reports a completed event. Both stay singular.
temas.titulo: Había vs hubo: imperfect vs preterite of haber
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish Había vs Hubo (Imperfect vs Preterite)

temas.regla: Empezar / comenzar (conjugated) + a + infinitive = to start doing. Always the a, always an infinitive, never a gerund.
temas.titulo: Empezar / comenzar a + infinitive: to start doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Empezar/comenzar a = to begin/start doing something (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: Tardar(se) / demorar(se) + time + en + infinitive: the person (or the vehicle) is the subject. Never me tarda or te tardó.
temas.titulo: Using tardar(se) / demorar(se) = to take time
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish verbs "tardarse/demorarse"= to take time

temas.regla: ¡Cuánto / cuánta / cuántos / cuántas + noun! expresses surprise at a quantity. It agrees with the noun and keeps its accent.
temas.titulo: Cuánto + noun in exclamations about quantities
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Cuánto + noun in exclamations about quantities in Spanish

temas.regla: Would like = indirect pronoun + gustaría (only this form) + infinitive: me gustaría, te gustaría, le gustaría, nos gustaría, les gustaría.
temas.titulo: Using gustar in the conditional = would like
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using gustar in the conditional in Spanish = would like [to do something]

temas.regla: Hace + length of time + que + preterite = how long ago: hace dos días que pasó. A length of time, never a date, between hace and que.
temas.titulo: Hace + time + que + preterite: how long ago something happened
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Use Hace + length of time + que + the preterite tense in Spanish to say how long ago something happened

temas.regla: Quedar = to be left / to arrange to meet (quedar con) / to end up (+ adjective). Quedarse = to stay / to keep (quedarse con). Quedarle = to fit, to suit / to have left (me quedan 20 pesos).
temas.titulo: Quedar, quedarse and quedarle: the different meanings of quedar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verbs Quedar, Quedarse and Quedarle (Different meanings of verb quedar)

temas.regla: Menos (never changes) = except: todos menos Beto. With pronouns use subject forms: menos yo, menos tú. For except that + sentence: excepto que / salvo que.
temas.titulo: Using menos to say except
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using "menos" to say except in Spanish

temas.regla: For a plan that is already decided, use ir a + infinitive. Estar + gerund is only for what is happening right now.
temas.titulo: Using the near future ir a (not the present progressive) for plans
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish near future (not the present progressive) for future arrangements

temas.regla: Llevar (present or imperfect) + time + gerund = have / had been doing for: llevo tres días estudiando. Negative: llevar + time + sin + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Using llevar + gerund to express how long an action has been going on
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using llevar + present participle to express duration of an action in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: Colloquially: estamos a + date / day of the week; estamos en + season. Always the nosotros form, in the present.
temas.titulo: Estar (not ser) for dates, days and seasons (colloquial)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ser vs Estar in Spanish: Use estar (not ser) to talk about dates, days of the week and seasons (colloquial)

temas.regla: O sea (casual) and es decir (formal) introduce a clarification or a consequence: in other words, that is, so. They never change.
temas.titulo: Using o sea / es decir to clarify, explain and express a consequence
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using "o sea/es decir" to clarify, explain and express a consequence in Spanish

temas.regla: What a + adjective + noun = ¡Qué + noun + más / tan + adjective! No article after qué; qué and más / tan never change; the adjective agrees.
temas.titulo: Exclamations: qué + noun + más / tan + adjective
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Exclamatory sentence in Spanish: qué + noun + más/tan + adjective

temas.regla: Tener (muchas) ganas de + infinitive = to feel like / to look forward to. Estar deseando + infinitive = to really look forward to, can't wait to.
temas.titulo: To look forward to: tener ganas de and estar deseando
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "to be looking forward" in Spanish with tener ganas and estar deseando

temas.regla: Terminar (conjugated) + de + infinitive = to finish doing. Acabar de can mean this too, but more often means to have just done.
temas.titulo: Terminar de + infinitive: to finish doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using terminar de+ [infinitive] = to finish doing something in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: The conditional expresses what you would do: wishes and intentions (me comería un taco) and advice (yo que tú, iría). Yo que tú = if I were you.
temas.titulo: Using the conditional for wishes, hypotheses and advice
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the conditional in Spanish to express hypothesis/wish/suggestion in the present or future

temas.regla: I think so = creo que sí / pienso que sí; I guess so = supongo que sí; I hope so = espero que sí. Never drop que, never drop sí / no.
temas.titulo: How to say I think so, I guess so, I hope so
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say I think so/I guess so /I hope so in Spanish

temas.regla: Gustar-type verbs work the same in every tense: indirect pronoun + verb in 3rd person, singular or plural to agree with the thing: me gustó / me gustaron, me molestaba.
temas.titulo: Gustar and similar verbs in past tenses
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verb gustar and similar verbs in past tenses

temas.regla: To lend = prestar (agrees with the lender): ¿me prestas…? To borrow = pedir prestado (prestado agrees with the thing): ¿te puedo pedir prestadas tus herramientas?
temas.titulo: To lend and to borrow: prestar and pedir prestado
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say to lend/to borrow in Spanish with prestar/pedir prestado

temas.regla: Contar = to count (numbers, things), to tell (a story, news), to count / matter (eso no cuenta), and contar con = to count on, to have.
temas.titulo: Different meanings of the verb contar
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Different meanings of the Spanish verb contar

temas.regla: Time: a principios de (beginning), a mediados de (middle), a finales de (end), plural and with no article. Space: al principio de, en medio de, al final de.
temas.titulo: Expressing the beginning and end of a period or a space
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing the beginning and end of a period or space in Spanish

temas.regla: Por un lado…, por otro lado… lists two ideas, often in contrast, sometimes just adding (also, besides). Por otro lado alone = on the other hand, besides.
temas.titulo: On the one hand, on the other hand, in addition: connectives
temas.titulo_kwiziq: How to say "on the one hand, on the other hand, in addition" in Spanish (connectives)

temas.regla: To offer or suggest (shall I / shall we…?), Spanish uses a question in the present, in yo or nosotros: ¿vamos?, ¿te ayudo? Never the future.
temas.titulo: Using the present to make suggestions: shall I…?, shall we…?
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the present tense in Spanish for making suggestions

temas.regla: Suggestions: ¿Por qué no + present? ¿Y si (no) + present? ¿Qué tal si (no) + present? Por qué no only takes the present.
temas.titulo: Making suggestions with por qué no…?, y si…?, qué tal si…?
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using por qué no/y si/ qué tal si for suggestions in Spanish

temas.regla: Pedir = ask for (things, favors, orders, someone to do something: pedir que + subjunctive). Preguntar = ask a question, ask for information; preguntar por = ask about someone.
temas.titulo: Pedir vs preguntar: two ways to ask
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verbs Pedir vs Preguntar (to ask)

temas.regla: Llevar = take someone / something somewhere, carry, wear, contain, lead to. Llevarse = take away with you, get along (llevarse bien / mal), get (a fright, a surprise).
temas.titulo: Llevar vs llevarse
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verbs Llevar vs Llevarse (pronominal verbs)

temas.regla: At an age: a los + age; since an age: desde los + age; until an age: hasta los + age. Always with los. A los 16 = cuando tenía 16.
temas.titulo: Using a / desde / hasta + age
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using a/desde/hasta + age in Spanish

temas.regla: To ask whose, to whom, with whom, for whom, put the preposition before quién / quiénes: ¿De quién es? ¿Con quién fuiste? Use quiénes when you expect more than one person.
temas.titulo: Asking about people with preposition + quién
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Asking questions about people with preposition + quién in Spanish

temas.regla: Dónde (accent) is a question or exclamation word, also in indirect questions: no sé dónde está. Donde (no accent) is a relative that introduces a clause: el pueblo donde nací.
temas.titulo: Dónde vs donde (with and without an accent)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between dónde and donde in Spanish (with and without a written accent)

temas.regla: Cómo (accent) = how, in direct and indirect questions and exclamations: no sé cómo se llama. Como (no accent) = as / like, or I eat (from comer).
temas.titulo: Cómo vs como (with and without an accent)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between cómo and como in Spanish (with and without an accent)

temas.regla: Cuál (singular) / cuáles (plural) = which, which one(s), in direct and indirect questions. Same form for masculine and feminine, always with an accent, never with an article (that's el cual, the relative).
temas.titulo: Using cuál / cuáles = which / what (interrogative pronouns)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using cuál/cuáles = which/what in Spanish (interrogative pronouns)

temas.regla: Cuándo (accent) asks when, in direct and indirect questions and exclamations: dime cuándo vienes. Cuando (no accent) links a time clause: me llamó cuando llegó.
temas.titulo: Cuándo vs cuando (with and without an accent)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between cuándo and cuando in Spanish (with and without an accent)

temas.regla: In indirect questions (no sé, dime, me pregunto...), qué keeps its accent. Qué + noun = which / what + noun, and never changes: no sé qué zapatos ponerme. Qué can also be followed by a verb or an infinitive.
temas.titulo: Using qué in indirect questions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using qué in Spanish indirect questions

temas.regla: Use por (not para) for an exchange or trade: cambiar pesos por dólares; te doy mi tabla por la tuya.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) for an exchange
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (and not para) in exchange for something

temas.regla: Use por (not para) for the means or channel: por teléfono, por correo, por avión (sending). To travel by vehicle, en is common: voy en avión.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) to express a medium or channel
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (not para) to express medium

temas.regla: Use por (not para) for the price you buy or sell something for: la vendí por tres mil pesos.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) to communicate price
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (and not para) to communicate price

temas.regla: Use por (not para) for distribution or sharing, meaning per / each: dos tacos por persona.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) for distribution: per, each
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (and not para) to express distribution or sharing

temas.regla: Use por (not para) for speed and rates: a 120 kilómetros por hora.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) to talk about speed
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (and not para) to talk about speed

temas.regla: Use para (not por) for a specific time, event or deadline: para Navidad, para tu cumpleaños, para el lunes. Por + event = because of it.
temas.titulo: Para (not por) for a precise time or occasion
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using para (and not por) for precise time location

temas.regla: Sí with an accent = yes (and the emphatic sí, sí mismo). Si without an accent = if (conditions) and whether (indirect questions).
temas.titulo: Sí vs si: with and without an accent
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between Sí and Si in Spanish (with or without accent)

temas.regla: Que without accent = that, which, who (connects). Qué with accent = what, how, in direct and indirect questions and exclamations.
temas.titulo: Qué vs que: with and without an accent
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between qué and que in Spanish (with and without an accent)

temas.regla: Debido a + noun = because of, due to; debido a que + full sentence (with a verb) = because. Debido a can be replaced by por.
temas.titulo: Debido a / debido a que: because of, due to
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using debido a / debido a que for because of / due to in Spanish

temas.regla: Más with an accent = more (comparisons, quantities, also plus). Mas without an accent = but, a formal, written synonym of pero.
temas.titulo: Más vs mas: with and without an accent
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between Más and Mas in Spanish (with or without a written accent)

temas.regla: Así que (so) and por lo tanto (therefore) introduce the result of the main clause. They take the indicative; the subjunctive appears only if you add a word of doubt or possibility (probablemente, puede que).
temas.titulo: Using así que / por lo tanto (result clauses)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using así que/ por lo tanto in Spanish (subordinate result clauses)

temas.regla: Y (and) becomes e before a word that starts with the sound i (i- or hi-): Marco e Inés, padres e hijos. Not before hie- (agua y hielo), and not at the start of a question (¿Y Isabel?).
temas.titulo: When the conjunction y becomes e
temas.titulo_kwiziq: When the Spanish conjunction y becomes e

temas.regla: O (or) becomes u before a word that starts with the sound o (o- or ho-): siete u ocho, mujeres u hombres. Before any other letter, o stays.
temas.titulo: When the conjunction o becomes u
temas.titulo_kwiziq: When the Spanish conjunction o becomes u

temas.regla: To say by whom or by what something was done, use por (never para), usually after a participle: un mural pintado por Diego Rivera.
temas.titulo: Por (not para) to say "by" someone or something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Por vs Para in Spanish: Using por (not para) to say "by" [whom/what]

temas.regla: O (u before o- / ho-) = or. To say either... or, repeat it: o... o... or o bien... o bien... The first o can be dropped, but never the second.
temas.titulo: Conjunctions o / u / o... o / o bien... o bien
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish conjunctions o/u/o...o/o bien...o bien (coordinating conjunctions)

temas.regla: Mientras que (whereas) and en cambio (on the other hand) introduce a contrasting clause, with the indicative. Mientras que can start the sentence; en cambio can't. Punctuation: , mientras que / ; en cambio,
temas.titulo: Using mientras que / en cambio for contrast
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using mientras que/en cambio for comparison/contrast in Spanish

temas.regla: In Spanish the preposition goes at the start of the question, before qué: ¿De qué hablas? (What are you talking about?). Never leave it at the end like in English.
temas.titulo: Asking questions with preposition + qué
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Asking questions with prepositions + qué in Spanish

temas.regla: Dentro de + length of time = in (time left until something happens): dentro de tres días. En + time = how long it takes: lo hice en media hora. Dentro de can also mean within / among in an abstract sense.
temas.titulo: Using dentro de for in / within / among (time and place)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using dentro de for in/within/among in Spanish (time/place)

temas.regla: Under something = debajo de (most common) or bajo (more formal, no de). Underneath / down here, with no object = debajo or abajo (adverbs). Bajo also means under figuratively: bajo presión.
temas.titulo: Prepositions bajo, abajo, debajo (de) meaning "under"
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Prepositions bajo, abajo, debajo (de) meaning "under"

temas.regla: Words ending in -e, -n or -r usually take -cito / -cita / -citos / -citas: calle → callecita, camión → camioncito, amor → amorcito.
temas.titulo: The diminutive suffix -cito, -cita with words ending in -e, -n and -r
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish diminutive suffix -cito, -cita, -citos and -citas with words ending in -e, -n, and -r

temas.regla: All nouns ending in -aje are masculine: el viaje, el equipaje, el mensaje. Plural: add -s (los viajes).
temas.titulo: Nouns ending in -aje are masculine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish nouns ending in -aje are masculine

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -ista and -crata have the same form for both genders; only the article changes: el / la dentista, los / las demócratas.
temas.titulo: Gender of nouns and adjectives ending in -ista and -crata
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender of nouns and adjectives ending in -ista and -crata in Spanish

temas.regla: Some nouns can be masculine or feminine with the same meaning; the speaker, the region or the register decides: el / la sartén, el / la mar, el / la azúcar, el / la tilde.
temas.titulo: Nouns with both genders and no change in meaning
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Some Spanish nouns have both genders without a change of meaning

temas.regla: Lo + masculine singular adjective = the … thing / what is …: lo bueno, lo difícil. Lo + adjective + de highlights a quality. Lo + adjective + ser: lo malo es que…
temas.titulo: The neuter article lo + adjective (+ ser)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using neuter article Lo + adjective + ser in Spanish

temas.regla: Nouns used in a general sense as the subject need the article in Spanish: el café, la salud, los perros. English leaves it out.
temas.titulo: When Spanish needs the definite article el, la, los, las
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Presence of the Spanish definite articles el/la/los/las

temas.regla: -azo, -ote, -ón make things bigger, often with admiration or scorn: perrazo, grandote, cabezón. -azo also means a blow with something: cabezazo, codazo.
temas.titulo: Augmentative suffixes: -azo, -ote, -ón
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish augmentative suffixes -azo, -ote, -ón

temas.regla: Nouns ending in -ez (abstract) and -eza are feminine: la niñez, la madurez, la belleza, la tristeza. Other -z nouns have no fixed rule.
temas.titulo: Gender of nouns ending in -ez and -eza
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Gender of nouns ending in -ez/-eza in Spanish

temas.regla: Talking about someone with señor, señora, señorita: use the article (el señor Ramírez). Talking to them: no article (Señor Ramírez, pase). Don / doña never take the article.
temas.titulo: Using the definite article or not with titles
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish definite article or not with titles

temas.regla: Most nouns ending in -ud are feminine and abstract: la salud, la actitud, la juventud. Plural: -udes. Exceptions: el ataúd, el laúd, el alud.
temas.titulo: Most nouns ending in -ud are feminine
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Most Spanish nouns ending in -ud are feminine

temas.regla: Fractions: cardinal + ordinal number like English (un cuarto, dos quintos); 1/2 = la mitad, 1/3 = un tercio; double = el doble. Plural when the top number is more than one.
temas.titulo: Expressing fractions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Expressing fractions in Spanish

temas.regla: Ordinals for events in a series: décimo, undécimo / decimoprimero, vigésimo, trigésimo… They agree in gender: la vigésima edición. In speech, cardinals are common after 10.
temas.titulo: Using ordinal numbers with events, celebrations and anniversaries
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using ordinal numbers with events, celebrations, anniversaries in Spanish

temas.regla: Se puede + infinitive = you can / one can; se debe + infinitive = you must / one must, talking about people in general. The verb is always third person singular.
temas.titulo: Using se debe / se puede to say you must / you can (impersonal)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using se debe/se puede to say You must/you can (impersonal sentences)

temas.regla: Affirmative opinion verbs (creo que, pienso que, me parece que) take the indicative. Make them negative (no creo que, no pienso que) and the verb after que goes in the subjunctive.
temas.titulo: The subjunctive with negative opinion phrases
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish subjunctive with negative opinion phrases

temas.regla: The conditional simple can express a guess about the past: Serían las tres = It was probably three. ¿Dónde estaría? = I wonder where he was. For a known fact, use the preterite or imperfect. For a guess about the present, use the future.
temas.titulo: The conditional to express probability about the past
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish conditional simple to express probability/speculation about the past

temas.regla: For a hypothetical or unlikely situation: si + imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional: Si tuviera más dinero, viajaría. Never si + present subjunctive.
temas.titulo: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional (hypothetical)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish imperfect subjunctive in hypothetical clauses introduced by si followed by the Spanish conditional simple

temas.regla: To hope that something happened or has happened, use esperar que + present perfect subjunctive (haya + participle): Espero que hayas llegado bien. Never the preterite or the present perfect indicative after esperar que.
temas.titulo: Esperar que + present perfect subjunctive (completed past action)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish present perfect subjunctive after esperar que to express a completed action in the past

temas.regla: Verb + tan + adjective/adverb + que = so... that...: cause first, then the result. The adjective agrees with its noun. Don't confuse it with tan... como (as... as).
temas.titulo: [verb] + tan + adjective / adverb + que = so... that...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using [verb] + tan + [adjective/adverb] + que to say "so... that..."

temas.regla: Verb + tanto/a/os/as + noun + que = so much / so many... that...: cause, then result. Tanto agrees with the noun. Don't confuse it with tanto... como (as much / many as).
temas.titulo: [verb] + tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + que = so much / many... that...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using [verb] + tanto/a/os/as + [noun]+ que = [verb] so much/many...that...

temas.regla: To say you like someone romantically, the person who is liked is the subject: Tú me gustas = I like you (lit. you are pleasing to me). Gustar is conjugated for that person: gusto, gustas, gusta, gustamos, gustan.
temas.titulo: Using gustar to express personal attraction
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verb gustar to express personal attraction

temas.regla: Este = this (present or near future): esta semana. Ese = that (past or future): ese día. Aquel = that, far in the past, often nostalgic: aquellos tiempos. Aquel is never used for the present or future.
temas.titulo: Demonstrative adjectives to refer to time
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish demonstrative adjectives to refer to time (present, past and future)

temas.regla: Al + infinitive = when / on / upon doing (time) or because of doing (cause). Al + haber + participle presents the action as already completed: al haber terminado = having finished / because he had finished.
temas.titulo: Al + infinitive / perfect infinitive = when doing / because of doing
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish conjunction al + infinitive/perfect infinitive = when doing/ because of doing [something]

temas.regla: A + infinitive gives a quick command to whoever is there: ¡A comer!, ¡A callar! Keep se with pronominal verbs (¡A lavarse las manos!), or use te. Not for negative commands.
temas.titulo: A + infinitive to give a command
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using preposition a + infinitive to express a command in Spanish

temas.regla: Seguir or continuar + gerund = to keep (on) doing: sigue lloviendo. No preposition and no infinitive in between. Seguir changes e > i (sigo, sigue).
temas.titulo: Seguir / continuar + gerund = to keep on doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verbs seguir/continuar + present participle = to keep on [doing something]

temas.regla: Ser + adjective + que (es necesario que, es mejor que, es raro que) and estar bien / mal que take the subjunctive. Expressions of truth or certainty (es verdad que, es cierto que, es un hecho que) take the indicative, unless they're negative.
temas.titulo: The subjunctive with impersonal expressions
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish subjunctive with impersonal expressions

temas.regla: Expressions of doubt or uncertainty take the subjunctive, affirmative or negative: dudo que, es posible que, es probable que, es imposible que, puede ser que. Certainty (estoy seguro de que, es cierto que) takes the indicative.
temas.titulo: The subjunctive to express doubt or uncertainty
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish subjunctive to express doubt or uncertainty

temas.regla: Verbs of wish or feeling (querer que, preferir que, desear que, me gusta que, me molesta que, me alegra que, me da igual que) take the subjunctive when the subject changes. Same subject: use the infinitive, without que.
temas.titulo: The subjunctive with verbs of wish and feeling
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish subjunctive with verbs that express "wish" and "feeling"

temas.regla: Estaba + gerund describes what was going on, often interrupted by another action. Estuve + gerund is an ongoing action inside a closed time frame: estuvimos bailando toda la noche, de 6 a 7.
temas.titulo: Imperfect progressive vs preterite progressive (was + -ing)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: The Spanish imperfect progressive vs the Spanish preterite progressive (was +ing)

temas.regla: Starting an exclamation with que + present tense gives a warning or a threat about the near future: ¡Que llegas tarde! ¡Que te dejo aquí! This que has no accent. A que reinforces it.
temas.titulo: Que to introduce a warning or threat
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using que to introduce a warning or threat in Spanish

temas.regla: Que (no accent) can introduce a reason, like porque, especially after a command or a statement: Me voy, que tengo que trabajar. It's informal and goes after the main clause.
temas.titulo: Que to express cause
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using que to express cause in Spanish

temas.regla: Could have done = pude / podía / podría + haber + participle. All three mean the same: there was a chance, and it didn't happen.
temas.titulo: Poder + haber + participle = could have done
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using poder to say could have [done something] in Spanish (modal verbs)

temas.regla: Preterite: a past action seen as complete, with a beginning and an end (abrió = the door is open). Imperfect: a past action seen in progress, with no clear start or end (abría = we watch it opening). English often translates both the same.
temas.titulo: Imperfect vs preterite (general use)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperfect vs the preterite in Spanish (general use)

temas.regla: Quería = wanted (a desire). Quise = tried to. No quería = didn't want to. No quiso = refused.
temas.titulo: Querer in the preterite vs the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using querer in the preterite vs the imperfect in Spanish

temas.regla: Pude = managed to, succeeded (we know the result). No pude = failed to. Podía / no podía = could / couldn't, the ability at that time, without saying how it turned out. Always + infinitive.
temas.titulo: Poder in the preterite vs the imperfect
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using poder in the preterite vs the imperfect in Spanish (could in past actions)

temas.regla: Quedarse + gerund = to stay doing, to carry on doing something, often starting at that moment: se quedó mirándome. Works in any tense. Always the gerund.
temas.titulo: Quedarse + gerund = to keep doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Quedarse + [gerund] = to do something continuously in Spanish (perífrasis verbal)

temas.regla: To become: convertirse en (a radical change), hacerse (profession, ideology, religion, also by effort), ponerse + adjective (temporary changes in mood, health, look), quedarse + adjective (a lasting result, often a loss).
temas.titulo: Convertirse en / ponerse / hacerse / quedarse = to become
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using convertirse en / ponerse / hacerse / quedarse to express "to become" (Spanish verbs of change)

temas.regla: Sería + adjective + que (sería bueno / mejor / genial / aconsejable que) is followed by the imperfect subjunctive: Sería genial que ganaran. Never the indicative or the conditional after que.
temas.titulo: Sería + adjective + que + imperfect subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the imperfect subjunctive in Spanish with impersonal expressions in the conditional (Sería+adjective+que)

temas.regla: Would have done = haber in the conditional (habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían) + participle. Nothing goes between habría and the participle. In many sentences hubiera can replace habría, but not the other way around.
temas.titulo: Habría + participle = would have done
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using haber to say would have [done something] in Spanish

temas.regla: He podido and pude both mean was able to / managed to. Present perfect: the time frame is still open or not mentioned (hoy, este mes). Preterite: a finished time (ayer, el año pasado). In Mexico the preterite is used much more, even for today.
temas.titulo: Poder in the present perfect and the preterite (could in the past)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using poder in the present perfect and the preterite for "could" in past actions

temas.regla: A gerund at the start of a sentence can mean while doing: Estudiando en la universidad, conocí a mi esposo. No preposition before it (never mientras + gerund). Mientras + conjugated verb means the same and is a bit less formal.
temas.titulo: The gerund to say while doing something
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish gerund to say while [doing something]

temas.regla: The third person plural without a subject can mean someone / people / they in general, when we don't know or don't care who did it: Dicen que..., Tocan la puerta, Me robaron la cartera.
temas.titulo: Impersonal sentences with the ellos form
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish impersonal sentences using the ellos form of the verb

temas.regla: Aunque + indicative: a fact you're stating, maybe new for the listener (although it IS raining). Aunque + subjunctive: something already known to both (even though), or something that may or may not happen (even if).
temas.titulo: Aunque + present indicative vs present subjunctive
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Aunque + the present indicative vs the present subjunctive in Spanish

temas.regla: Esperar que + haya + participle can express a hope that something will be done by a future point: Espero que lo hayas decidido antes del lunes. There's usually a future reference (para entonces, antes de..., el lunes).
temas.titulo: Esperar que + present perfect subjunctive (completed action in the future)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the Spanish present perfect subjunctive after esperar que to express a completed action in the future

temas.regla: ¡Qué poco + verb! = how little / how rarely (poco never changes): ¡Qué poco duermes! ¡Qué poco/a/os/as + noun! = how little / how few, agreeing with the noun: ¡Qué pocos amigos tiene! Qué always has an accent.
temas.titulo: ¡Qué poco! to express surprise about a small amount
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Qué poco/s + verb/noun to express surprise about a small quantity or infrequency

temas.regla: Era: background description, time frame not important. Fue: the situation is seen as complete, within a limited time, or as a summary of an event (el viaje fue increíble).
temas.titulo: Ser in the imperfect vs the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verb ser in the imperfect vs the preterite

temas.regla: Estaba: a state in the past, no interest in when it ended; it may still be true. Estuvo: a state seen as over, often with a time limit (estuvo enfermo una semana).
temas.titulo: Estar in the imperfect vs the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verb estar in the imperfect vs the preterite

temas.regla: Tenía = had (possession or state as background, no limits). Tuvo = had in a closed period, or got / received / had an event: tuvo un bebé, tuve un examen, tuvo un accidente.
temas.titulo: Tener in the imperfect vs the preterite
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verb tener in the imperfect vs the preterite

temas.regla: Deber + infinitive = must (obligation); also accepted for assumptions. Deber de + infinitive = must (assumption, probably), never obligation. For the past: debió de / debe de haber + participle.
temas.titulo: Deber vs deber de (obligation and assumption)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish modal verb Deber versus Deber de (obligation and assumption)

temas.regla: For accidents and unplanned events: se + indirect pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les) + verb agreeing with the thing: se me cayó el celular, se le cayeron las llaves. It takes the blame off the person.
temas.titulo: The accidental se with an indirect object pronoun
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the "accidental" reflexive (se) with an indirect object pronoun

temas.regla: To say how long something had been going on at a past moment: hacía + length of time + que + imperfect. Or: imperfect + desde hacía + time. Often followed by cuando + preterite.
temas.titulo: Hacía + time + que + imperfect = had been doing for
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Hacía + length of time + que + the Spanish imperfect tense to express duration in the past

temas.regla: Volverse + adjective or noun = to become, to turn, for changes in someone's character or attitude, usually lasting and not on purpose: se volvió muy desconfiado.
temas.titulo: Volverse to express to become / to turn
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish verb volverse to express to become/to turn (verbs of change)

temas.regla: Antes de / después de / luego de + infinitive = before / after doing. With haber + participle (the perfect infinitive), the action is stressed as completed: después de haber terminado. Pronouns attach to haber.
temas.titulo: Antes de / después de / luego de + haber + participle
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Antes de/Después de/Luego de followed by haber + participle in Spanish

temas.regla: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive. Después de que / luego de que: indicative for present habits and past events (past subjunctive also possible), subjunctive for the future.
