temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using the pluperfect subjunctive after the conjunction como si (subordinate manner clauses)

temas.regla: Que + present subjunctive, with no main verb, has three uses: a wish (¡Que te vaya bien! = I hope it goes well), an insistent repeated order (¡Que te comas la sopa! = I said eat your soup!), and an indirect order for someone else (Que lo haga Juan = let Juan do it).
temas.titulo: ¡Que + subjunctive! = wishes and repeated orders
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using que + the present subjunctive in Spanish to to express a wish/command

temas.regla: With preferir, the second thing compared is introduced by a, not que: Prefiero el café al té. Even with clauses: Prefiero que me digas la verdad a que me mientas. Que only appears as part of the content (prefiero que...). With people's names the first personal a can drop: Prefiero (a) Pedro a Nicolás.
temas.titulo: Preferir A a B: prefiero el mar a la montaña
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Spanish verb Preferir a vs Preferir que

temas.regla: De + tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + que / como + indicative gives the cause: from so much...: de tanta gente que había. De + tan + adjective/adverb + que / como: de tan cansado que estaba. De tanto + infinitive also works: de tanto gritar = from shouting so much.
temas.titulo: De tanto / de tan ... que = because of so much...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using de tan/tanto + que/como to express a cause (subordinate causal clause)

temas.regla: De + infinitive can replace a si clause: De ser verdad = si es verdad. Tenses are shown by the main verb and by the infinitive form: de poder (if I could), de haber sabido (if I had known), de ser aprobada (if it is passed), de no llegar (if we didn't get there).
temas.titulo: De + infinitive = if...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: De + infinitive (subordinate conditional clause)

temas.regla: Por mí (que) + present subjunctive = I don't mind if..., it's fine by me (indifference or even approval): Por mí, que se vayan. Para mí que + indicative = I have a feeling that..., I reckon: Para mí que va a llover. One shows your permission; the other your hunch.
temas.titulo: Por mí, que... vs para mí que...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Difference between por mí que and para mí que

temas.regla: A + noun often says how something is done: means (a pie, a caballo, a mano, a nado), abruptness or force (a patadas, a empujones, a gritos), the way an action unfolds (a ciegas, a tragos, a oscuras), and style (a la mexicana, a la plancha).
temas.titulo: A for how something is done: a pie, a mano, a gritos
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using preposition "a" to indicate how/in which style something is done

temas.regla: Conque (one word) introduces a consequence, often followed by a command: Estás tosiendo, conque tómate el jarabe. At the start of a question or exclamation, it shows surprise: ¿Conque ya no tienes dinero? = So you're out of money? In Mexico, así que is far more common; conque sounds a bit old-fashioned or literary.
temas.titulo: Conque = so, therefore (colloquial)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using conque to express therefore/so

temas.regla: Como + subjunctive can mean if, usually in a warning, threat or worried prediction: Como no estudies, vas a reprobar. It always takes the subjunctive here. Como + indicative at the start of a sentence means since, because: Como no estudiaste, reprobaste.
temas.titulo: Como + subjunctive = if (warnings and threats)
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using como+ subjunctive as "if" (subordinate conditional clause)

temas.regla: Ya sea + A + o + B offers two options, any of which works: whether..., or..., either... or...: Paga ya sea en efectivo o con tarjeta. Use ya fuera for the past. Variants: sea... o..., sea... sea..., fuera... fuera...
temas.titulo: Ya sea... o... = whether... or..., either... or...
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Ya sea/ya fuera... o... to express whether... or...

temas.regla: Ante is a formal preposition for place, not time: before, in the presence of (ante un juez, ante notario). It also means faced with, in the face of (ante la crisis, ante la duda). Ante todo = above all. For time, use antes de.
temas.titulo: Ante = before, in front of, faced with
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using Spanish preposition ante

temas.regla: In compound tenses, the passive uses haber + sido + participle: ha sido construido, había sido vendida, habrán sido elegidos. Sido never changes; the main participle agrees with the subject. The agent comes with por.
temas.titulo: Passive in compound tenses: ha sido construido
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the Spanish passive voice with ser + participle (Compound tenses - passive voice)

temas.regla: The progressive passive is estar + siendo + participle: El paciente está siendo atendido = is being treated. Estar changes tense; siendo never changes; the participle agrees with the subject. Compound progressive: ha estado siendo investigado.
temas.titulo: Passive in progressive tenses: está siendo + participle
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Forming the Spanish passive voice with progressive tenses (passive voice)

temas.regla: Ni or ni siquiera = not even. After a negative verb: No tenía ni (siquiera) una cobija. At the start, no other negative is needed: Ni siquiera me saludó. Ni is more colloquial; ni siquiera is more emphatic. Also ¡Ni modo! = oh well, no way around it.
temas.titulo: Ni / ni siquiera = not even
temas.titulo_kwiziq: Using negative conjunction ni/ni siquiera in Spanish
